chapters.title: Chapter 601: The Price of Knowing
paragraphs: Leon spent his first two days in Moonfall walking, asking questions, and buying almost nothing.

He started in the outer markets, where ordinary citizens shopped. A bowl of noodles cost eight copper. A clean room above a teahouse cost twenty copper a night, while a better inn inside the third ward asked nearly twice that. Clothes, cart fare, common medicine, and meals all remained affordable if a person knew the proper price.
Cultivator goods used a different scale.

The exchange houses bought low-grade spirit stones and sold them back at a clear profit. Leon visited three before he understood what the pouch Shen Baoyuan had given him was worth. Combined with the ordinary silver, it could support him modestly for about a year if he avoided expensive pills and artifacts.

One clerk tried to explain the exchange rate as though Leon had never handled money. Leon let him. The explanation included service fees, purity deductions, and the fact that chipped stones were weighed rather than counted. None of those details appeared on the rate board outside.

At the next exchange house, Appraisal showed that its testing tray consistently judged purity slightly lower than it should. Leon left without using it. The third house displayed its inspection formation openly and charged a fixed fee. He wrote down the address.
The family had provided that security the morning after losing twelve people.
Leon did not insult them by trying to return it. He simply revised his understanding of the gift and remembered what they had done.

He bought a copper meridian chart, a basic breathing manual, and small samples of spirit stone from several sources. Appraisal identified differences in purity, but it could not explain why one merchant’s stones worked better with a particular formation ink. That required knowledge of local crafting methods.
The limitation pleased him. It meant there was something real to learn.

He also bought three thumb-sized beast-core fragments from different stalls. All carried denser energy than comparable materials from Velaria, yet each had been processed differently. One still held a trace of hostile instinct that could contaminate a careless formation. Another had been washed so thoroughly that much of its useful energy was gone. Appraisal revealed the results, but the merchants’ answers taught him which methods caused them.
On the third morning, the pill market opened before sunrise.

Leon priced Qi Restoration Pills at eleven stalls. The common version was cheap and came loose in ceramic jars. Appraisal described a small, rapid replenishment followed by impurities that would build up with repeated use.
At the twelfth stall, he asked for a better grade.
The alchemist behind the counter had burn scars along both forearms. She looked at his temporary registration jade and then at his clothes.
"Which sect or clan account should I place the order under?"
"Neither."
"An introduction from an established alchemist?"
"No."
She tapped one of the common jars. "Then this is what I can sell you."
"The better medicine isn’t sold publicly?"

"It is sold. It simply has buyers before it reaches the shelf." She gestured toward the market. "A sect receives pills through its medicine hall. A clan maintains contracts. A known cultivator gets introduced by someone whose reputation can pay for his mistakes. Everyone else attends an auction and spends several times the proper price."
Leon bought three common pills and a written guide to their ingredients.
He asked about pills used to strengthen meridians. The alchemist named two, then refused to sell either without first examining his circulation.
"A pill that widens healthy channels can tear damaged ones," she said. "I will not sell medicine to a stranger who cannot tell me what is inside his own body."
Leon thanked her and did not argue. Her caution told him the legitimate alchemists understood that stronger medicine carried stronger risks.
The conversation explained more than the medicine. Moonfall’s best resources moved through relationships. Money mattered, but identity decided which doors opened.
Yanning joined him on the fourth day.
Her family still had losses to settle, so Leon had not asked for her time. She appeared outside the guest wing after breakfast with a ledger under one arm.
"You asked three servants where the formation district was," she said. "They each gave you different directions."
"One route may eventually reach it."
"Come with me before you end up in the tannery ward."

The formation district followed the western canal. Leon spent the morning studying devices that would have transformed life in Velaria and barely drew attention here. Formation lamps fed on ambient qi. Heat stones kept pots simmering without flame. Purification arrays cleaned public cisterns. Paired communication jades carried voices across the city.
Their basic functions were easy to understand. The construction was not.
At a stall selling formation flags, a broad man in a leather apron offered Leon a set of six for nine silver each.
"Four each," Yanning said.
The merchant frowned. "These are ash-wood."
"They are pine stained to resemble ash-wood. The veins were painted after carving, and the third flag will fail first in wet weather."
The man looked at Leon, then back at Yanning. "Five."
"Four, or we leave."
Leon bought the six flags for twenty-four silver.
Once they were outside, he said, "You cut the price by more than half."
"He saw your temporary jade and decided you were an easy sale."
"I would have discovered the problem eventually."
"After paying him fifty-four silver."
Leon could not argue with that.

Yanning stayed with him through three more shops. She showed him which seals indicated a licensed craftsman, warned him away from ores treated to imitate a higher grade, and arranged for a scripture seller to reserve several beginner texts until Leon could inspect them.
Her questions appeared naturally throughout the errands.
"Did your inheritance use formation flags?"
"Some rooms had fixed arrays."
"And nobody taught you to maintain them?"
"Most of what I learned came from surviving mistakes."
She accepted the answer even though it explained very little.

Leon appreciated her skill. She gathered information without repeating herself and never pushed hard enough to make refusal awkward. He assumed she was building a connection with a potentially valuable cultivator. That explanation was sensible and incomplete.

Before returning to the compound, they stopped at a herb seller. Leon chose seeds, two living roots wrapped in damp moss, and a hardy potted herb whose energy density exceeded anything common in Velaria.
"Planning a garden?" Yanning asked.
"I want to know whether plants from this region will grow in unfamiliar soil."
"The roots might. The seeds are safer." She checked the wrapping around the pot. "Keep the samples separate. Some spirit herbs poison weaker plants simply by sharing water."
That was exactly the kind of local knowledge Appraisal had not provided.
Back in his room, Leon placed the purchases beside the cultivation texts. The pile looked unimpressive, yet each piece answered a question or helped him ask a better one.

He still had no intention of taking a spiritual-root test. Three shops offered them, and two had lines of parents waiting with their children. Until Leon knew what the artifacts measured and recorded, he would not let anyone point one at his foreign foundation.
For the moment, observation was safer.

He sorted the day’s purchases into three groups. The first could be studied inside his room. The second needed isolation before entering his dimensional world. The last group, including the pills, would remain sealed until he understood how local qi interacted with his body.
Yanning had saved him money, but more importantly, she had shown him which questions he had failed to ask. Leon added those questions to the front page of his notes.
Tomorrow, the public archive would teach him what these people believed a cultivator’s body was supposed to contain.

chapters.title: Chapter 602: What the Higher World Builds
paragraphs: The public archive charged two silver for a day’s access.
Leon chose a cultivation primer written for children.

The text compared the body to a country. The spiritual root gathered energy from the world. Meridians carried it inward, and the dantian stored and refined it into qi the cultivator could control. Without open meridians, even a powerful spiritual root had nowhere useful to send what it gathered.

The later Chapters described what happened when those structures grew together. Meridians widened and became harder to damage. The dantian changed in quality as well as capacity. At higher stages, the cultivator’s spirit and energy became woven tightly enough that destroying flesh no longer guaranteed death.
That last section was simplified for children, but Leon recognized the beginning of the path that eventually produced a cosmic anchor.
Leon read the section twice.
They build an additional structure inside themselves.

Local cultivation did more than increase the same attributes measured by the System. It created a second foundation: roads, reservoirs, filters, and a circulation network designed over countless generations.

Leon’s own power entered through his two hearts and the framework of his class. His body had no spiritual root, dantian, or proper meridians. The method worked, but it skipped every stage these cultivators used to compress and refine their energy.
He could not copy their system blindly. He needed to understand what advantages it produced and find a way to answer them through his own foundation.

He copied the diagrams instead of trusting himself to remember them. Later, he could compare them with anatomy from Velaria and ask Loriel whether living beings inside his world showed any dormant equivalent. Even a failed comparison would narrow the problem.
The same books helped him place Moonfall’s experts.

Most citizens never cultivated. Many who began stopped within the lower realms and worked as guards, artisans, or caravan hands. Golden Core cultivators received respect anywhere in the city. Dao Palace experts, whom the System recognized as Archons, could protect a regional family by themselves.

Void Immortals stood much higher. They served as supreme elders, ancient ancestors, and the foundations of influential organizations. Resources meant for them cost more than many merchant families earned in years.
Above them were Earth Immortals, the local equivalent of Ethereal Lords.
Qingyue belonged somewhere within that greater realm.
Leon left the archive near sunset with copied notes and three more introductory manuals.

Outside, a group of young cultivators stepped aside for an elderly man wearing a plain brown robe. Nothing about his clothes marked him as wealthy, but the pressure contained beneath his skin made the System identify him as an Archon. Shopkeepers bowed as he passed. A formation hall closed its front doors so he could inspect a commission in private.
Nobody announced his rank. The street’s behavior did it for him.
That evening, he prepared the herb samples.

He did not open a passage inside the Shen guest wing. Instead, he used the private connection to his dimensional world and routed the sealed package directly into an empty quarantine plot far from inhabited ground. The roots, seeds, and potted herb remained separated behind layered barriers.
Loriel inspected them there. Her answer returned through the same connection the next morning.
"The roots are alive, and the seeds should germinate. The potted one is stronger than most medicinal plants we have cultivated. Send a small soil sample, but keep it sealed until I test it."

Leon purchased soil from the same seller, divided it into several containers, and transferred only one. Nothing would enter the dimensional world’s farms until Loriel confirmed it carried no pests, spores, or harmful energy.
The precautions cost little. A careless contamination could cost far more.
Later that morning, Leon visited the street outside Moonfall’s largest auction house.

Formation lamps burned white above the entrance. Sedan chairs arrived without joining any queue, and guards bowed when they recognized the crests on their passengers’ robes. Leon watched an Archon cross the threshold without being searched while a wealthy merchant waited outside with three attendants and a sealed chest.
The merchant was eventually admitted only after an auction official came out to vouch for him.
Leon had enough money to enter the public sales. The private rooms required a recognized name, an introduction, or goods valuable enough to make the auction house interested.
That distinction appeared everywhere once he knew how to see it.

Moonfall had shops for ordinary people, shops for independent cultivators, and an almost invisible trade serving the organizations that ruled the region. The best goods rarely reached an open counter.

By the sixth day, Leon had learned enough to begin planning. The city offered resources that could improve cultivation, medicine, formation work, and food production inside his dimensional world. Access would take time. He needed trusted contacts and a better understanding of what he could safely sell.
The Shen compound also changed that day.

Two inner courtyards closed before noon. Guards left the warehouse rotation and took positions around the rear grounds. Servants stopped using one covered walkway and began taking the longer route through the kitchens.
Yanning crossed the guest courtyard twice carrying documents. Both times, she walked faster than usual.
Leon noticed and did not question her. The Shens had given him a map that clearly marked their private areas. Their hospitality did not entitle him to family secrets.
Nothing suggested immediate danger. The guards appeared alert rather than frightened, and the household continued its normal work.

At dinner, Leon heard two servants mention that the rear kitchens would remain closed through morning. One complained about carrying water around the long route. The other told him to lower his voice and follow the steward’s instructions. Neither sounded as though an attack was expected.

Late that night, Leon sat on the floor of his room with the meridian chart spread before him. A spirit-stone fragment rested in his palm while he compared its natural circulation with the routes engraved into the copper.
Then something crossed the wall of the third ward.
Leon felt four disturbances moving through the night. Each was smooth and controlled, as if the air had forgotten to resist them.
The System responded a moment later.
[Ethereal Initiate — Early Stage]
[Ethereal Initiate — Early Stage]
[Ethereal Initiate — Early Stage]
[Ethereal Initiate — Late Stage]
Leon lowered the stone.
Any one of those cultivators could serve as the ancestor of a lesser organization. Four of them were crossing a merchant ward together with their presences concealed.

He considered the alarm bell in the caravan yard and rejected it. If they were targeting the Shens, an alarm might send them through the household before ordinary guards could react. If their objective lay elsewhere, sounding it would expose Leon before he understood the situation.
He extinguished the lamp and suppressed his aura until it blended with the room.
A short spatial fold carried him onto the guest-wing roof without disturbing a tile.
The four intruders entered over the eastern storehouse. They passed through a weak seam in the wall formation, waited for a patrol at exactly the right moment, and moved as soon as it turned away.
They knew the estate’s layout and its schedule.
Leon followed from the rooftops, keeping twenty paces between them.

The intruders crossed the outer grounds without triggering a ward. At the first inner gate, their leader placed a flat disc against the stone. The formation dimmed just long enough for all four to pass.
Beyond it waited the sealed courtyards Leon had noticed that afternoon.
The intruders headed straight toward them.

chapters.title: Chapter 603: The Guests No One Invited
paragraphs: Leon followed without attacking.

Stopping the intruders near the outer wall would protect the household, but it would tell him nothing about why four Ethereal Initiates had entered a merchant estate. He needed to know their objective and whether more were waiting outside.

The raiders moved with practiced discipline. Their Late-stage leader carried the flat disc in one hand. Whenever a ward blocked their route, he used the artifact to quiet it for a few breaths. The method had been prepared for the Shen estate’s formations.

The first two men carried no visible clan insignia. Their robes were dark, plain, and loose enough to hide weapons. Even their boots had been wrapped to soften the sound of each step. Whoever sent them wanted no clue left behind if an ordinary servant happened to see them.

At a junction near the family residence, the chain wielder paused and counted beneath his breath. A patrol crossed the far end of the passage three breaths later. The raiders moved behind it without being seen.
Their knowledge extended beyond the layout. They knew the household’s timing.
Near the rear garden, one of the Early-stage cultivators glanced toward the closed courtyards.
"The refinement should continue for at least two more hours."
"Then stop wasting time," the leader replied.
"If the old man senses the outer ward fall—"
"He won’t interrupt. If he closes himself off now, the treasure will discharge into his anchor. He loses the resource and may lose his foundation with it."
The leader stopped beneath a stone arch and faced the other three.
"Once we reach the chamber, keep your attacks away from the refinement array. The treasure must remain intact. Break the door and walls if necessary. Leave the extraction to me."
"And the old man?"
"He is already near the end of his life. Pulling the treasure away will finish what age started."
The spearman frowned. "The report said the family shifted guards this morning."
"They are protecting a secret they believe no one discovered," the leader said. "If they suspected us, the old man would never have begun the refinement."
"What about the girl who returned with the caravan? She handled the purchase accounts."
"She is below us, as is her father. Kill anyone who reaches this garden. We leave the rest asleep."
That was enough for Leon to understand the outline.

The Shens had bought a resource capable of strengthening a cosmic anchor and accelerating an Ethereal Initiate’s cultivation. Their Peak Ethereal Initiate ancestor was old and running out of time. A stronger anchor would improve his chance of reaching Ethereal Lord and gaining a longer life, though it could not guarantee the breakthrough.
The family had spent a large part of its wealth on one final attempt.

The clan behind these four had learned about the purchase and waited until the ancestor began refining it. He could not leave seclusion without risking his anchor, the treasure, and his last opportunity.

Leon heard nothing proving how the information had escaped. A purchase that valuable would leave traces through sellers, transfers, and the family’s finances. An influential clan might uncover the refinement date without help from inside the estate.
The reference to a report suggested careful surveillance, yet it answered nothing by itself. Leon would need one of them alive if he wanted the source.
The raiders entered the rear garden.
A dry ornamental pond filled its center. Six stone steps descended beyond it to a warded door built into the earth. The stone around the entrance radiated heat.

Two concealed formations guarded the final steps. The leader disabled the first with his disc. The second resisted long enough for energy to gather along the arch, but one of the Early-stage raiders placed three prepared needles into exact points along its edge. The light faded.
They had brought a different answer for every defense.
Behind the door, an immense circulation moved with slow precision. An old existence had opened its cosmic anchor as far as it dared and was drawing power from the treasure into its foundation.
The Shen guards could do nothing against the four people in this garden. Calling them would only create casualties and risk disturbing the refinement.
Leon sealed the arch behind the raiders with hardened space. He placed three layered barriers across the chamber entrance, each designed to absorb force without pressing against the door itself.
Then he stepped into view at the top of the stairs.
All four intruders turned.
The leader recognized him first. "The outsider from the caravan."
One of the others nodded. "The Shen family brought him through the eastern gate."
The leader studied Leon, then glanced toward the arch behind him. His expression sharpened when he sensed the spatial seal.
"You don’t understand whose business you’ve entered," he said. "Return to your room. The Shen family discovers a loss in the morning, and you remain uninvolved."
He wanted the theft kept quiet. That meant the clan could not act as openly as his threat suggested.
"The Shens gave me shelter, money, and papers when I had nothing in this world," Leon said. "I’m not moving."
The leader waited a moment, perhaps hoping Leon would reconsider.
"Remove him," he ordered. "I’ll open the chamber."
The three Early-stage Ethereal Initiates spread out as they climbed the steps.

They fought nothing like the cultivators who had attacked the caravan on the road. The difference went beyond their higher cultivation. Their qi remained compressed until the instant they used it, and they formed a practiced triangle without speaking. One carried a short spear. Another unwound a chain from his forearm. The third approached empty-handed through the center.
The leader returned to the door, but he kept part of his attention on the fight while setting his disc against the outer ward.
"Thirty breaths," he said. "If he is still standing, force him against the chamber barrier. I’ll use the impact to open both."
That order removed any doubt that the man was willing to risk the refinement if a clean theft became impossible.
The center attacker reached Leon first.
His palm carried enough force to crush the stairway. Leon stepped inside the strike and drove lightning through the man’s chest. The body burst apart under the impact.
Death did not follow.
The man’s consciousness and energy rushed away from the ruined manifestation, drawing upon an existence anchored throughout the cosmic background. A new body began forming several paces behind Leon.
Light revealed the active connection. Ice slowed the energy travelling through it, and Leon folded the surrounding space until every route back to the world passed through his control.
He severed the connection while destroying the forming body.
The distributed anchor collapsed with nothing left to sustain its identity. The cultivator’s presence vanished from the garden.
For a breath, even the chamber’s wards seemed loud.
The spearman and chain wielder stopped.
At the chamber door, the leader pulled his disc free and turned around. He no longer treated Leon as an inconvenience.
"He can destroy the anchor connection," the spearman said.
"I know."
The leader pressed both hands against the disc. Lines of clan-script ignited across its surface, and the ward around the chamber groaned.
"Keep him away from me," he ordered. "Use everything."
The remaining two attacked together as the leader began forcing the breach.

He needed to know their objective and whether more were waiting outside.
The raiders moved with practiced discipline.

Whenever a ward blocked their route, he used the artifact to quiet it for a few breaths.
The method had been prepared for the Shen estate’s formations.

Even their boots had been wrapped to soften the sound of each step.
Whoever sent them wanted no clue left behind if an ordinary servant happened to see them.

A patrol crossed the far end of the passage three breaths later.
The raiders moved behind it without being seen.

If he closes himself off now, the treasure will discharge into his anchor.
He loses the resource and may lose his foundation with it."
The leader stopped beneath a stone arch and faced the other three.
"Once we reach the chamber, keep your attacks away from the refinement array.
The treasure must remain intact.
Break the door and walls if necessary.
Leave the extraction to me."
"And the old man?"
"He is already near the end of his life.
Pulling the treasure away will finish what age started."
The spearman frowned.
"The report said the family shifted guards this morning."
"They are protecting a secret they believe no one discovered," the leader said.
"If they suspected us, the old man would never have begun the refinement."
"What about the girl who returned with the caravan?
She handled the purchase accounts."
"She is below us, as is her father.
Kill anyone who reaches this garden.
We leave the rest asleep."
That was enough for Leon to understand the outline.

Their Peak Ethereal Initiate ancestor was old and running out of time.
A stronger anchor would improve his chance of reaching Ethereal Lord and gaining a longer life, though it could not guarantee the breakthrough.
The family had spent a large part of its wealth on one final attempt.
The clan behind these four had learned about the purchase and waited until the ancestor began refining it.
He could not leave seclusion without risking his anchor, the treasure, and his last opportunity.

A purchase that valuable would leave traces through sellers, transfers, and the family’s finances.

The leader disabled the first with his disc.

The light faded.
They had brought a different answer for every defense.
Behind the door, an immense circulation moved with slow precision.
An old existence had opened its cosmic anchor as far as it dared and was drawing power from the treasure into its foundation.
The Shen guards could do nothing against the four people in this garden.
Calling them would only create casualties and risk disturbing the refinement.
Leon sealed the arch behind the raiders with hardened space.
He placed three layered barriers across the chamber entrance, each designed to absorb force without pressing against the door itself.

chapters.title: Chapter 604: The One Left Alive
paragraphs: Chapter 604: The Fourth Anchor
The spearman drove toward the chamber while the chain wielder attacked Leon from the side.

Their plan was simple. One would force Leon to protect the door, leaving the other free to strike him. The leader continued feeding power into the breaching disc, and fine cracks spread across the chamber’s outer ward.
Leon raised an ice wall across the steps. The spear pierced it in two blows. Before the third, Leon folded the distance beneath the attacker’s feet.
The man completed his charge at the bottom of the dry pond, twelve paces from his target. Ice closed around his legs.

The chain wielder used the opening. Qi-hardened links struck Leon’s shoulder and tore through cloth and flesh before he caught them. Lightning ran along the metal. The attacker released the weapon, but the current had already reached his arm and disrupted its circulation.
Leon crossed the space between them and broke the man’s manifestation with a second strike.
The cultivator abandoned his body before it fully failed. His anchored consciousness reached beyond the sealed garden, attempting to form a new avatar on the far side of the wall.
Leon bent the route back into the containment field.
The new body assembled directly in front of him. Light showed the active connection, and Leon severed it before the avatar could stabilize.
The second presence disappeared.
The spearman shattered the ice around his legs. He looked at the two empty places where his companions had died, then compressed everything he had into one final charge at the chamber.
Leon caught him one step from the door.

The spearhead punched into Leon’s already wounded shoulder, but space twisted the weapon away before it could pass through. Leon drove lightning down the shaft and through the spearman’s spine. Ice locked the collapsing body in place while Leon cut the connection sustaining it.
The third anchor failed.
Leon pulled the spear free. Light closed the wound, leaving the shoulder stiff and sore.
The garden fell quiet.
Three Early-stage Ethereal Initiates were dead. None had escaped, and the chamber remained sealed.
The Late-stage leader removed the breaching disc from the damaged ward and stored it inside his robe. Pressure unfolded from him until cracks spread across the frozen pond.
"You allowed us to enter," he said.
"I needed to know why you came."
The leader sealed the garden with a clan technique, blocking the passage in both directions. "Then you know enough to understand what happens if my clan learns you interfered."
"Your clan wanted a quiet theft. You gave me the chance to walk away because you didn’t want witnesses or questions."
The man’s expression changed slightly. Leon had his answer.
They moved at the same time.

The first compressed sheet of qi shattered Leon’s ice barrier and reduced the stone behind it to gravel. The second arrived through the opening. Leon folded aside, then sent lightning through the leader’s footing to break his balance.

The leader recovered before the current finished passing through him. He turned the disrupted step into a low sweep that split the stone where Leon landed. Leon blocked the follow-up with layered ice, and the impact drove cracks through all three layers.

The difference between Early and Late stage was clear. The leader’s body carried denser energy, and his cosmic anchor restored damage almost as quickly as Leon inflicted it. Twice Leon struck through his chest. Both wounds closed as the wider anchored existence supplied a new manifestation.
Killing him would have been easier. Leon needed him alive.

Lightning disrupted his techniques just before they settled. Ice narrowed the battlefield and suppressed his channels without destroying them. Light let Leon track every injury while layers of space remained over the ancestor’s chamber.
The leader realized Leon’s intention when a third strike stopped short of his dantian.
"You want information."
He threw the breaching disc.
It tore through two spatial barriers and struck the third. The circulation behind the chamber door trembled once.
Leon’s restraint vanished.
Space compressed across the lower garden. The leader tried to cross nine paces and travelled only two. His next attack curved away from the chamber and buried itself in the dry pond.
Unable to break free, he abandoned his body.
His manifestation collapsed. Consciousness rushed into the distributed cosmic anchor, intending to reform beyond the estate.
Leon wrapped the active connection in folded space and closed it into a loop. He left the anchor intact. Everything the leader sent outward returned to the same few paces of garden.
A new body formed inside the compression.

The leader tried again and reappeared in the same place. On the third attempt, he stopped trying to flee. His awareness turned inward, reaching for his own anchor with enough force to damage it and destroy whatever information Leon wanted.
Leon tightened the spatial restraint around the connection. The leader remained linked to his anchor but could no longer reach deeply enough to collapse it.
Ice entered his limbs and major channels. Lightning disrupted his nerves. Guided by Light, Leon applied only enough force to suppress the body and keep the man conscious.
The leader ended on his knees with his arms locked at his sides. His avatar was intact, his anchor remained stable, and he could neither reform elsewhere nor destroy himself.
Four minutes later, Leon removed the seal from the garden arch.
Six guards rushed through first. Shen Baoyuan followed in a night robe, with Yanning beside him holding two formation flags. They stopped when they saw the garden.
Baoyuan counted the three bodies and stared at the kneeling prisoner.
"Four Void Immortals," he said quietly. "Inside my home."
"Three are permanently dead," Leon said. "The Late-stage leader is restrained. He knows who sent them and whether another group is coming."

Yanning descended the steps and placed one hand against the stone beside the chamber door. The refinement circulation continued on the other side. When she confirmed it, some of the tension left her shoulders.
"What did you hear?" she asked.

"The treasure strengthens a cosmic anchor. Your ancestor is refining it because this may be his last chance to reach Earth Immortal." Leon nodded toward the prisoner. "They learned the date and waited until he couldn’t safely interrupt the process."
"Was someone inside the family involved?"
"Their conversation didn’t prove that. A purchase this valuable could be traced from outside. He should know how they found out."

Yanning turned to the guards and began issuing orders. The inner estate was to be sealed. No one would enter the rear garden. Every guard on the eastern route would be questioned, but nobody would be accused without evidence. The prisoner would be moved only after Leon approved the restraints.
Shen Baoyuan remained near the arch, looking from Leon to the sealed chamber.
"I gave you money and a token," he said. "That cannot repay this."
"You gave me enough to live here for a year when I had no local money, papers, or place to sleep." Leon looked at the old merchant. "I remembered."
Baoyuan bowed his head and did not argue.
Leon crouched in front of the captured leader. He checked the spatial loop, the restrained connection, and the stability of the cosmic anchor. Everything held.
The man raised his head. Fury remained in his eyes, but the confidence had disappeared.
"Who sent you?" Leon asked.
The captured leader let Leon’s question hang in the cold garden air.
"You should think carefully about what you’ve done," he said at last.

His voice remained steady, though maintaining it took visible effort. Leon had left him kneeling at the foot of the steps, his arms locked against his sides and every path to his Ethereal foundation held inside a spatial restraint.
"Three members of my force are permanently dead," the man continued. "That is not a debt the Shen family can settle with an apology."
"I didn’t ask what I should fear," Leon said. "I asked who sent you."

The leader turned toward Yanning. She sat near the covered walkway with a lamp beside her and a writing board across her knees. Trusted guards had sealed the surrounding courtyards, but none stood close enough to hear.

"You manage the routes and ledgers," the prisoner said. "Then you understand what happens when a merchant family offends a power it cannot fight. Your house has warehouses in other cities and caravans on roads you cannot protect. Release me, and I can report that the treasure became impossible to extract. Keep me, and the people behind me will eventually learn where I disappeared."
Yanning’s brush paused, then resumed.
"How long have you been a Void Immortal?" Leon asked.
The change of subject unsettled the man. "Three hundred and eleven years."
"Then you know what happened to the other three."

chapters.title: Chapter 605: Three Hours Until Dawn
paragraphs: Leon crouched in front of him and adjusted the spatial restraint.

For two seconds, every route connecting the prisoner’s manifested body to the wider structure of his existence closed. Leon did not touch or damage the Ethereal foundation itself. He merely made it unreachable.
The leader’s face emptied of color.
Leon released the pressure before any harm was done.
"Your foundation is intact," he said. "I intend to keep it that way. Tell the truth, and you remain alive as a prisoner. Deliberately lie, and I lose my reason to preserve you."
The man breathed slowly until the panic left his eyes.
"You need what I know."
"That is why you’re still breathing."
Silence stretched between them.
"Qiao," the prisoner finally said. "The Qiao clan of Ninefold Ridge."
Yanning’s brush stopped.
"Their mark?" she asked.
"A notched iron ring. There is one sewn inside my collar."

Yanning looked at Leon. "The clan is based eleven days east when the roads are clear. They control three mining valleys and much of the river trade beyond them. They have no seat in Moonfall, but they buy through local intermediaries and have several Void Immortal ancestors."
"Powerful enough to crush the Shens?" Leon asked.

"If we challenged them openly and stood alone, yes." Her expression tightened. "A prisoner’s statement and an emblem won’t be enough for a formal accusation. They would deny everything, petition Moonfall’s magistrates, and demand restitution for damaging their name."
She turned the writing board around and drew a rough line east from Moonfall.

"Ninefold Ridge is far enough away that people here sometimes forget its reach. But Qiao ore enters Moonfall through several companies, and more than one ruling house depends on that trade. If we accuse them tonight, half the city will ask what proof we have. The other half will ask how much business they might lose by believing us."
"And the Qiao clan will learn exactly how much you know," Leon said.
"Yes. Silence gives us room to investigate. An accusation gives them warning."
Leon returned his attention to the prisoner. "How did they learn about the treasure?"
The answers came slowly.

The Qiao clan had noticed the Shen family selling routes, collecting old debts, and moving an unusual amount of wealth through brokers. That activity revealed the purchase. Someone along the delivery chain had then marked the treasure itself with a tracking formation fine enough to survive the Shen family’s inspection.

The formation did not transmit conversations or images. It revealed the treasure’s location and changes in its energy. When Shen Yuanhe began refining it, the paired device reacted. The Qiao clan knew the exact moment their target became both active and difficult to move.
"That was why you attacked tonight," Leon said.
"The old man couldn’t stop safely. If he interrupted the process, he would ruin the treasure and injure his foundation. We expected the rest of the estate to be helpless."
"You expected correctly," Yanning said. "Except for one guest."
The prisoner ignored her.
"How were you meant to leave?" Leon asked.
"Across the eastern storehouse and through the same seam we used to enter. We would leave Moonfall before anyone knew what had happened."
"Then report after you were clear?"
"There was no need. We were expected at a rendezvous."
Yanning looked down at her notes.
"No confirmation method?" she asked.
"None."
"My family sends a receipt runner with herb shipments worth three silver. The Qiao clan sent four Void Immortals after a foundation treasure and arranged no one to check whether they succeeded?"
The prisoner did not answer.
Leon watched his breathing.
"Someone local has the paired device," he said. "That person watches the estate and reports if you fail to appear."
The leader’s jaw tightened.
Leon touched the restraint again without closing it. The man felt the warning and lowered his eyes.
"One agent," he admitted. "He will take position an hour before dawn. If we reach the rendezvous, he leaves without sending anything. If we don’t, he reports what he sees."
"Where?"
"He chooses his own observation point."
"How does he contact the clan?" Yanning asked.
"A paired message-jade. He also holds the device linked to the tracker."
"Does he know your route out?" Leon asked.
"Only the rendezvous beyond the eastern gate."
Yanning recorded the answer. "Then he cannot confirm where the team went afterward. That gives us something to work with."
The leader glanced between them. "A false message will not fool him if the tracker still shows the treasure inside this estate."
"Then we change what the tracker shows," Leon said.
The eastern sky was still dark, but it would not remain so for long.
Yanning checked the small water clock a servant had placed beside her. "Less than three hours."

Leon looked toward the chamber beneath the garden. The vast circulation within continued at the same slow rhythm. Shen Yuanhe had no idea that four Void Immortals had crossed his walls, and stopping now could still destroy his final chance.
Capturing the observer before he reports only delays the problem until the clan misses two groups instead of one.
"If no message arrives, Ninefold Ridge investigates immediately," Leon said.
"And if the agent reports that we vanished inside the estate, they’ll know the Shens had help," Yanning replied.
"Then we don’t stop the report."
She studied him. "What do we do?"
Leon looked down at the man who had spent the last hour trying to bargain his way out of the garden.
"We decide what it says."
They prepared the false report in the strongroom beneath the counting house.
The captured leader was chained to a formation post. Yanning wrote each version of the message on thin paper, read it aloud, and burned it when either Leon or the prisoner found a flaw.
"It must be short," she said. "The longer it is, the more chances we give him to notice something wrong."
"Short and ordinary," Leon agreed.

The message would claim the raid had succeeded. The treasure had been secured, but an unexpected patrol near the eastern route had forced the group to hide outside Moonfall. They would suppress the tracker, remain concealed, and make contact again after attention faded.
It explained why the four Void Immortals would miss their rendezvous without suggesting that anything inside the Shen estate had defeated them.

The leader surrendered the necessary details one at a time. The contact method used two paired message-jades and worked within a limited distance. Authentication came from a rotating monthly phrase disguised as ordinary commercial news. That month’s opening concerned the price of dried river fish in Baihe.
"That is the Qiao clan’s secret code?" Leon asked.
"Complicated codes are forgotten under pressure," the leader said. "This one is remembered."
The tracker was harder to deceive.

Its formation remained on the treasure while Shen Yuanhe refined it. Removing the mark could disturb the process, and Leon refused to risk that. Instead, he found the faint signal leaving the underground chamber and folded a thin layer of Space around it. The sheath reduced the signal without touching its source. sentences.text: Leon crouched in front of him and adjusted the spatial restraint.
For two seconds, every route connecting the prisoner’s manifested body to the wider structure of his existence closed.
Leon did not touch or damage the Ethereal foundation itself.
He merely made it unreachable.
The leader’s face emptied of color.
Leon released the pressure before any harm was done.
"Your foundation is intact," he said.
"I intend to keep it that way.
Tell the truth, and you remain alive as a prisoner.
Deliberately lie, and I lose my reason to preserve you."
The man breathed slowly until the panic left his eyes.
"You need what I know."
"That is why you’re still breathing."
Silence stretched between them.
"Qiao," the prisoner finally said.
"The Qiao clan of Ninefold Ridge."
Yanning’s brush stopped.
"Their mark?" she asked.
"A notched iron ring.
There is one sewn inside my collar."
Yanning looked at Leon.
"The clan is based eleven days east when the roads are clear.
They control three mining valleys and much of the river trade beyond them.
They have no seat in Moonfall, but they buy through local intermediaries and have several Void Immortal ancestors."
"Powerful enough to crush the Shens?" Leon asked.
"If we challenged them openly and stood alone, yes." Her expression tightened.
"A prisoner’s statement and an emblem won’t be enough for a formal accusation.
They would deny everything, petition Moonfall’s magistrates, and demand restitution for damaging their name."
She turned the writing board around and drew a rough line east from Moonfall.
"Ninefold Ridge is far enough away that people here sometimes forget its reach.
But Qiao ore enters Moonfall through several companies, and more than one ruling house depends on that trade.
If we accuse them tonight, half the city will ask what proof we have.
The other half will ask how much business they might lose by believing us."
"And the Qiao clan will learn exactly how much you know," Leon said.
"Yes.
Silence gives us room to investigate.
An accusation gives them warning."
Leon returned his attention to the prisoner.
"How did they learn about the treasure?"
The answers came slowly.
The Qiao clan had noticed the Shen family selling routes, collecting old debts, and moving an unusual amount of wealth through brokers.
That activity revealed the purchase.
Someone along the delivery chain had then marked the treasure itself with a tracking formation fine enough to survive the Shen family’s inspection.
The formation did not transmit conversations or images.
It revealed the treasure’s location and changes in its energy.
When Shen Yuanhe began refining it, the paired device reacted.
The Qiao clan knew the exact moment their target became both active and difficult to move.
"That was why you attacked tonight," Leon said.
"The old man couldn’t stop safely.
If he interrupted the process, he would ruin the treasure and injure his foundation.
We expected the rest of the estate to be helpless."
"You expected correctly," Yanning said.
"Except for one guest."
The prisoner ignored her.
"How were you meant to leave?" Leon asked.
"Across the eastern storehouse and through the same seam we used to enter.
We would leave Moonfall before anyone knew what had happened."
"Then report after you were clear?"
"There was no need.
We were expected at a rendezvous."
Yanning looked down at her notes.
"No confirmation method?" she asked.
"None."
"My family sends a receipt runner with herb shipments worth three silver.
The Qiao clan sent four Void Immortals after a foundation treasure and arranged no one to check whether they succeeded?"
The prisoner did not answer.
Leon watched his breathing.
"Someone local has the paired device," he said.
"That person watches the estate and reports if you fail to appear."
The leader’s jaw tightened.
Leon touched the restraint again without closing it.
The man felt the warning and lowered his eyes.
"One agent," he admitted.
"He will take position an hour before dawn.
If we reach the rendezvous, he leaves without sending anything.
If we don’t, he reports what he sees."
"Where?"
"He chooses his own observation point."
"How does he contact the clan?" Yanning asked.
"A paired message-jade.
He also holds the device linked to the tracker."
"Does he know your route out?" Leon asked.
"Only the rendezvous beyond the eastern gate."
Yanning recorded the answer.
"Then he cannot confirm where the team went afterward.
That gives us something to work with."
The leader glanced between them.
"A false message will not fool him if the tracker still shows the treasure inside this estate."
"Then we change what the tracker shows," Leon said.
The eastern sky was still dark, but it would not remain so for long.
Yanning checked the small water clock a servant had placed beside her.
"Less than three hours."
Leon looked toward the chamber beneath the garden.
The vast circulation within continued at the same slow rhythm.
Shen Yuanhe had no idea that four Void Immortals had crossed his walls, and stopping now could still destroy his final chance.
Capturing the observer before he reports only delays the problem until the clan misses two groups instead of one.
"If no message arrives, Ninefold Ridge investigates immediately," Leon said.
"And if the agent reports that we vanished inside the estate, they’ll know the Shens had help," Yanning replied.
"Then we don’t stop the report."
She studied him.
"What do we do?"
Leon looked down at the man who had spent the last hour trying to bargain his way out of the garden.
"We decide what it says."
They prepared the false report in the strongroom beneath the counting house.
The captured leader was chained to a formation post.
Yanning wrote each version of the message on thin paper, read it aloud, and burned it when either Leon or the prisoner found a flaw.
"It must be short," she said.
"The longer it is, the more chances we give him to notice something wrong."
"Short and ordinary," Leon agreed.
The message would claim the raid had succeeded.
The treasure had been secured, but an unexpected patrol near the eastern route had forced the group to hide outside Moonfall.
They would suppress the tracker, remain concealed, and make contact again after attention faded.
It explained why the four Void Immortals would miss their rendezvous without suggesting that anything inside the Shen estate had defeated them.
The leader surrendered the necessary details one at a time.

Authentication came from a rotating monthly phrase disguised as ordinary commercial news.
That month’s opening concerned the price of dried river fish in Baihe.
"That is the Qiao clan’s secret code?" Leon asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 606: The Lie That Went East
paragraphs: The rest of the estate had to look normal.

Yanning kept the rear garden sealed without increasing the guards on the outer wall. The kitchen fires were lit on schedule. Servants crossed the yards carrying water and ledgers. At first light, a cart of dyed cloth rolled out through the western gate because the same cart left every ninth morning.
From the street, the Shen estate remained an exhausted merchant household recovering from a caravan attack.
Leon left through a concealed spatial fold and emerged four streets away. He circled the compound once before noticing a man in a rented upper room above a noodle shop across from the eastern wall.

The location offered clear sight of two gates and three escape routes. The observer looked like a thin, middle-aged clerk in plain brown robes. His cultivation was far below the four raiders’, but his qi had been compressed so carefully that an ordinary sweep might have passed over him.

He had prepared the room well. Fine powder covered the inner threshold to expose an invisible intruder. A thread ran from the window latch to a bell beneath the table. Two coats hung beside different exits, allowing him to change his appearance before reaching the street.
He was not a fighter sent to survive a Void Immortal. He was an observer expected to notice trouble early and disappear.
The paired tracking device rested in a shallow bowl of water near the window.
Leon took position on the roof of a tannery across the street and waited.

The agent checked the device four times. Each time, his expression grew more uneasy. When the city watch began changing shifts and no one approached the rendezvous, he sat at the table and started writing.
Not yet.
At the eighth mark, the message-jade in his sleeve warmed.
The man stopped writing. He listened to the recorded message twice, then lifted the paired device from the bowl and examined the weakened signal.
The treasure appeared alive, active, and concealed.
Relief loosened his shoulders.
He burned his first draft, wrote a shorter report, pressed his token to the jade, and transmitted it east.
Leon waited until the light faded from the jade. He counted several more breaths to ensure the entire message had gone through.
Then he moved.
The agent sensed him before he reached the window. He fled across the roof tiles and dropped into the alley beside the noodle shop.
He knew the district. Under ordinary circumstances, that might have saved him.
Leon folded the nearest routes.

The agent turned left and emerged in the same enclosed courtyard he had just crossed. He tried the passage behind a stone well and returned to the courtyard again. On the third attempt, he stopped and stared at the walls as he realized the streets no longer led where they should.
His hand shot inside his robe.
Ice locked his feet and wrist. A narrow thread of lightning passed through his arm, forcing his fingers open before he could crush the destruction seal in his palm.

Leon stepped into the courtyard and confiscated the seal, three message-jades, the paired tracker, a fire talisman meant to destroy everything the agent carried, and a narrow knife hidden inside his boot.
"Who are you?" the man asked.
"Someone who needed you to send that report."
Leon carried him back through a concealed fold. No one on the street saw either of them leave.

The agent was placed in the disused eastern cellar, far from the strongroom holding the Void Immortal. Different guards watched the two rooms, and neither prisoner could sense or communicate with the other.
"We can compare their answers later," Yanning said as she secured the final formation. Tiredness showed beneath her eyes, but her hands remained steady. "The report bought us days."
"Days with a deadline," Leon said. "Eventually they’ll expect the treasure."
"Then we move what we can, trace everyone who handled the delivery, and strengthen the estate before that deadline arrives."
She began listing warehouses and trade routes under her breath, but stopped after the third name.
Leon had already turned toward the rear garden.

The strained circulation beneath the estate had changed. For two days, it had carried the uneven pull of something being forced uphill. Now the strain was gone. A slower and steadier rhythm had replaced it.
Yanning ran.
They reached the six stone steps together. The three dead raiders remained covered, and the cracked garden stones still bore the marks of the battle.
Below them, the sealed chamber door moved for the first time since the refinement began.
It opened from the inside.
The man who emerged from the chamber was still old.

Shen Yuanhe’s thin body remained stooped, and his hair was so pale it resembled smoke. He leaned against the doorframe for a moment before climbing the steps. No light spilled from him, and no phenomenon appeared above Moonfall.
The change lay deeper.

Before the raid, Leon had sensed instability throughout the old man’s existence. His Ethereal foundation had been slowly deteriorating, forcing it to spend more with every manifestation and recover less. That loss had stopped. The foundation was still ancient and worn, but it had become stable again.
The treasure had succeeded.
It had not turned him into an Earth Immortal.
Shen Yuanhe reached the top of the steps and saw the three covered bodies.
"How many?" he asked.
"Four entered the estate," Yanning answered. "Three are dead. The fourth is sealed beneath the counting house. We also captured their local observer."
The old man looked at her.
"Void Immortals, Great-Grandfather. Three Early-stage and one Late-stage."
For several breaths, Shen Yuanhe said nothing.

He walked to the nearest body and lifted one corner of the covering cloth. The dead cultivator’s ruined manifestation no longer carried even the faint pull of a surviving foundation. Shen Yuanhe checked the other two before lowering the cloths again.
"Permanent," he murmured.
The word carried more weight from him than it had from Yanning.

chapters.title: Chapter 607: The Debt He Chose to Pay
paragraphs: He had spent centuries in the same realm as the dead and understood precisely what should have allowed them to return.
"They came for the treasure."

"Yes. It was marked with a tracking formation before delivery. We have found no evidence that anyone inside the household betrayed us, and the tracker was enough to reveal when you began refining it."
His gaze moved to the chamber door. "Did they reach it?"

"No." Yanning gestured toward Leon. "He detected them crossing the third ward and followed until he confirmed their objective. He permanently killed three, captured the leader, and kept the chamber untouched. Then he used their dawn observer to send Ninefold Ridge a false report saying the theft succeeded."
"The refinement never faltered," Shen Yuanhe said.
"Not once."

The old man looked back at the open door. "I felt pressure against the outer wards near the end, but the treasure had already joined too deeply with my foundation. Had I stopped to investigate, I would have torn both apart."
His hand closed around the head of his walking stick.
"So I remained below and trusted people who did not know I was trusting them."
Shen Yuanhe studied Leon.

The examination was careful rather than forceful. Leon kept the surface of his power unchanged: a wandering cultivator from a collapsed inheritance realm, possessing four known affinities and a cultivation method no one here recognized.
The old man did not discover the dimensional world or Leon’s hidden abilities. Whatever questions the inspection created, he kept them to himself.
"Both of you should come inside," Shen Yuanhe said. "I have spent two days underground. I would prefer to hear the rest while sitting down."
They entered a small room beside the family court. A servant brought tea and withdrew. Shen Baoyuan joined them a few minutes later, exhausted from keeping the household calm through the night.
Shen Yuanhe drank half a cup before addressing Leon.
"What did protecting this family cost you?"
"A wound in my shoulder. It has healed."

"You know that is not what I mean." The old man set down the cup. "You permanently killed three Void Immortals. I have witnessed such deaths only a few times. Why did you risk yourself for people you had known less than a week?"
Leon had expected the question.

"Your family helped me when I had nothing useful in this world," he said. "No local papers, no registration, no money I could spend, and almost no knowledge of the region. Your grandson gave me enough to live modestly for about a year on the morning after he buried twelve of his own people. Your great-granddaughter spent her time teaching me which merchants could be trusted and which questions I should ask."
Yanning lowered her eyes to her tea.
"I could repay that help," Leon continued. "So I did."
"You could have allowed the raiders to take the treasure, then stolen it from them outside the city," Shen Yuanhe said. "No one here would have known."
"I considered it."
"And?"

"You would have sensed them extracting it and interrupted the refinement. You might have died, and the treasure could have been ruined. I would gain a damaged resource by letting the person using it die." Leon shook his head. "That was never worth doing."
"Even though you had no obligation to us?" Shen Baoyuan asked.
Leon looked at him. "You had no obligation to give a nameless stranger shelter or enough local money to survive. You chose to do it anyway."

Baoyuan’s mouth opened, then closed. The caravan losses were still visible in the lines around his eyes. Leon had not forgotten that the merchant’s kindness came during one of the worst mornings his family had endured.
Something in the old man’s expression eased.
The conversation turned to Ninefold Ridge.

The Shens could not accuse the Qiao clan publicly. The prisoners and notched-ring emblems were useful intelligence, but not proof of who had issued the command. Any Moonfall magistrate willing to accept Qiao influence could dismiss the raiders as independent thieves.

The false report created a window. Before it expired, the family could move vulnerable stock, review the broker chain, identify everyone who had handled the treasure, and rebuild the damaged formations with workers unconnected to the delivery.
Shen Baoyuan asked what should be done with the prisoners.
"They live," Shen Yuanhe said. "Separately sealed. No one questions either without me, Yanning, or Leon present."
"They tried to kill you," Baoyuan said.
"And now they can tell us how the Qiao clan hides agents, communicates, and selects targets. Revenge can wait until their information is exhausted."
The decision was final.

Shen Yuanhe ordered that the dead raiders be documented before their remains were destroyed. Their clothing, storage rings, weapons, and emblems would be catalogued separately. Nothing bearing a Qiao mark would be sold in Moonfall, where an interested buyer might trace it back to the estate.

"Keep copies in three places," he told Yanning. "One here, one with a factor outside the city, and one sealed where even I cannot reach it alone. If this is forced into the open later, memory will not be our only evidence."
Yanning added the order to her board.
Shen Yuanhe looked at Leon again.
"I could offer you silver or spirit stones. A large amount by my family’s standards."
"But?" Leon asked.

"But you have already learned the limits of money in Moonfall. A purse buys meals, rooms, and whatever reaches the public stalls. It does not buy trust, private knowledge, or access to resources whose owners never display them."
The old man rose carefully. When Yanning moved to support him, he tested his balance and waved her back.
"I have all three," he said. "I will not ask you to join my family or bind yourself to our problems. This is repayment, nothing more."
He walked to the door, then glanced over his shoulder.
"Come. I will show you why coin is the smallest part of what we owe."

chapters.title: Chapter 608: What Money Cannot Buy
paragraphs: The Shen family’s private archive occupied a long, low room behind the counting house. Shielded lamps hung between shelves of maps, route records, cultivation notes, and histories that had never appeared in Moonfall’s public bookshops.
Shen Yuanhe walked slowly, but his steps grew steadier as they continued.
"Where does Moonfall truly stand?" Leon asked. "People in the market speak as if every important road ends here."

"For most of them, it does," the old man replied. "Moonfall is a frontier gate. Resources from the Three-Moon Desolation pass through us before becoming wealth elsewhere. That makes the city valuable, not supreme."

Four major houses divided most of Moonfall’s authority. They controlled the gates, auctions, large formations, and contracts that kept trade moving. Yet none wanted a direct conflict with a regional power such as Ninefold Ridge.

Shen Yuanhe opened a map and indicated the roads leaving the city. The southern routes ended at controlled entrances to the Desolation. The eastern road divided toward the Qiao mining valleys and the river settlements beneath their influence. Farther north, larger cities handled goods Moonfall could only appraise and resell.
Jade Moon Palace lay beyond all of them, across the Eastern Jade Sea rather than within the frontier marches.
The distances made Leon revise his sense of scale. Moonfall felt vast because it gathered everything nearby. On the regional map, it was one useful gate among many.

"The city houses will act if open war threatens their streets," Shen Yuanhe explained. "They will not eagerly investigate a secret attack on one merchant family, especially when the accused clan can make the matter expensive."
"So the Qiao clan expected its raid to remain invisible."
"That was the reason it could afford to send four Void Immortals."
Leon paused beside a shelf of regional maps. "Void Immortals are rare here."

"Very. In a minor sect, one may be the ancestor whose name protects every disciple. In a family like mine, one is the reason rivals negotiate instead of taking. Ninefold Ridge risked four because it believed my refinement had left this estate defenseless and that no survivor would identify them."
Their disappearance would matter. The false report prevented an immediate reaction, but the clan would eventually demand the treasure or direct contact from its team.
Leon had understood that already. What he needed was knowledge the market primers had not provided.
"Explain the Ethereal, or you say Immortal foundation," he said.
Shen Yuanhe selected a thin wooden case and placed it on a reading table. Inside lay several hand-drawn diagrams of a human figure surrounded by widening rings.

"When a cultivator becomes a Void Immortal, the body stops containing the whole of his existence," he said. "The Immortal foundation distributes that existence through the world around him and supports the body he manifests. Destroy the body, and the foundation constructs another."
"What separates an Early-stage Void Immortal from a Peak one?"

"Depth, stability, and control. An Early foundation is newly formed. Rebuilding is slow, expensive, and disruptive. At Late stage, the connection is strong enough that a cultivator can lose a manifestation and return without surrendering the entire battle. At Peak, the foundation has reached the broadest state available before Earth Immortal."
The old man touched one of the outer rings on the diagram.

"But time still matters. Repeated damage leaves strain. Centuries of rebuilding leave wear. My foundation had been weakening for years. Medicine could sustain my body, but the body was not the source of the decline."
"The treasure repaired that damage."

"It repaired and reinforced what I already possessed. My future cultivation will be faster, and I now have more time to seek the next step." Shen Yuanhe closed the case. "It did not give me the understanding required to become an Earth Immortal. That breakthrough cannot be purchased by gathering enough energy."
Leon compared the explanation to the System’s terms.
Ethereal Initiate. Ethereal Lord.
The System gave him ranks and levels. Shen Yuanhe had explained why two people within the same rank could differ so greatly in recovery and control.
Leon’s own foundation had developed through another path. He could not assume that local cultivation methods would strengthen it safely.
I need to understand the differences before I let anyone inside the dimensional world experiment with this.
Shen Yuanhe answered several more questions, then handed Leon a thin wafer of dark jade. The Shen emblem was carved into one face, with smaller markings around its edge.

"This is an inner-network token," he said. "Show it to one of our factors in Moonfall or the five other cities marked on the back. It grants access to private sale lists, honest authentication, and the prices we offer trusted partners. My people can also introduce you to craftsmen who refuse unknown clients."
Leon turned the token over. "Can it be used for discreet transactions?"
"For small batches. You may buy or sell without your name appearing at both ends of the record. Larger transactions attract attention no token can remove."
"Can I request something through one city and collect it in another?"
"If our routes connect them. You pay transport, insurance, and local taxes. The token ensures the request is handled by people whose reputations my family guarantees."

That mattered almost as much as the private lists. Leon could not personally verify every formation component, medicinal plant, or cultivation text. A reliable chain of appraisers reduced the chance of buying something altered, tracked, or falsely identified.
"What authority does it grant over your people?"

"None. It does not make you a Shen, open our warehouses, or protect you from Moonfall’s laws." A hint of amusement crossed the old man’s face. "Yanning said you would ask about the limits before thanking me."
"She was right." Leon slipped the token into his sleeve. "Thank you."
"Use it well. That will be thanks enough."
The token alone was worth more than another purse. It opened the hidden part of the market Leon had spent six days trying to find.
Shen Yuanhe led him through a reinforced door at the back of the archive. Three separate formations examined the old man’s identity before the locks released.

The treasury beyond was smaller than Leon expected. Weapons rested in sealed racks. Talismans filled lacquered cases. Crystals and ore samples sat beneath glass covers marked with dates and appraisals.
Shen Yuanhe ignored the brightest objects.
He stopped before a ceramic pot standing alone on a stone plinth. A small formation surrounded it, maintaining a steady flow of earth energy.
"You may choose a weapon if you prefer," the old man said. "But this is what I intended to offer."
He lifted the lid.
Inside grew a low fern with leaves so dark green they appeared black. Its roots crossed a bed of faintly luminous soil, and every patch they touched looked richer than the soil around it.
Leon leaned closer.
The plant was not impressive in the way a sword or defensive treasure might be.
It was alive.
"What is it?" he asked.
"An Earthmarrow Fern," Shen Yuanhe said. "And if you are as sensible as I hope, you will understand why it is worth more than anything shining behind you."

chapters.title: Chapter 609: A Root for Another World
paragraphs: Leon examined the dark fern without touching it.
"What does it do?"
"Nothing quickly," Shen Yuanhe said. "It will not raise your cultivation, heal a wound, or protect you from an attack."
He removed the ceramic pot from its formation and set it on a lower table so Leon could see the roots through a narrow crystal panel in the side.

"A mature Earthmarrow Fern draws scattered earth qi from its surroundings and converts it into a form other living things can absorb. The process is slow, but continuous. Given ten years, the ground around it becomes suitable for valuable herbs. Given several decades, it can turn poor land into a true cultivation field."
"Can it be harvested?"

"Two fronds in a season, safely. They form the base of several pill formulas and regrow if the plant remains healthy. Greedy owners cut too much, weaken the roots, and kill what took generations to mature."
"Can it reproduce?"
"Rarely. It produces seed only after enriching its surroundings beyond a certain point. Under ordinary conditions, that takes close to a century. Most owners harvest it to death long before then."
Leon studied the root system again.

Loriel’s Child of Life class did not guarantee success with a plant from a higher world. But she understood living energy better than anyone else he knew, and the dimensional world offered controlled land that could be isolated from every existing field.
One fern might become several. Even if it never reproduced, improving the soil around it could benefit generations of medicinal plants.
"How long has your family kept this one?" he asked.
"Four generations. We have taken almost nothing from it."

Shen Yuanhe showed him the family record. Every harvested frond had a date, a purpose, and a note about the plant’s recovery. Some entries were separated by years. The Shens had used it only when a medicine could not be made another way.

"We tried three times to move it into prepared ground," the old man said. "Each time, the roots began rejecting the local qi before the first day ended. Returning it to this soil saved it. Since then, we have treated the pot as its home."
"Then moving it anywhere is a risk."
"Yes. That is why the record matters more than the stories surrounding the plant."
"And you’re giving it to me?"

"You protected the refinement that may have given me many more years," Shen Yuanhe said. "The fern has spent decades in this pot because we possess no uncontaminated land worth planting it in. Keeping it alive has preserved its value, but it has helped no one."
He gestured toward the weapon racks.
"If you would rather have something useful in battle, choose it. I will not be offended."
Leon barely looked at the weapons.
"I’ll take the fern."
Yanning, who had followed them into the treasury, glanced from him to the plant. "You already have somewhere to grow it?"
"I have a cultivation project that may suit it."
It was true and revealed nothing.

Shen Yuanhe nodded without pressing. "Then take the archive record as well. It contains every successful feeding cycle and every mistake my family documented. Do not plant it beside anything valuable until you know how it reacts."
"I won’t."
Back in the guest wing, Leon waited until he was alone and every privacy formation was active.
He did not open a passage.

Through the private connection that already linked him to the dimensional world, he drew the sealed pot out of the room without creating a visible aperture or releasing a pulse of spatial energy into the estate. The fern appeared inside a quarantine plot Xyra had prepared in the eastern flats, three hundred paces from the nearest cultivated field.
The plot contained bare soil, layered barriers, and separate water channels. Nothing would leave it until Loriel understood exactly what the fern consumed and produced.
Loriel examined the pot before allowing anyone to break its protective seal.

Xyra kept the quarantine barriers closed while Loriel used thin strands of life energy to inspect the fern without feeding it. They tested water from three parts of the dimensional world on separate samples of its original soil rather than pouring anything into the pot. Even the air inside the enclosure was introduced gradually.
"It’s healthy," she reported later. "Older than Shen Yuanhe implied, too. The roots have been pruned several times, but carefully."
"Can you propagate it?"
"Maybe."
The cautious answer told Leon more than an easy promise would have.

"I need to test the soil first," Loriel continued. "Then its energy intake, its water needs, and how it responds to this world. If I move it straight into our fields and it reacts badly, I lose the plant and might damage everything around it."
"How long before you know?"

"Weeks before I understand the basics. Months before I risk a cutting." Her voice softened. "But the soil inside the pot is changing exactly as the old man described. If it adapts, it could be very useful."
"Could it damage the dimensional world?"

"Anything living can damage the wrong environment if introduced carelessly. That is why it stays sealed." Loriel paused. "So far, it is drawing only a small amount of earth energy. It is not spreading roots or releasing seed. Those are good signs, but they are only the first signs."
"Tell me before you change anything."
"I will. And send the full record, not a summary. Whoever kept this plant alive knew enough to be cautious."
"I’ll send you the Shen records."
Leon ended the connection and looked at the empty place where the pot had stood.

The fern offered no immediate increase in power. That was precisely why it had been overlooked in a treasury containing weapons and talismans. Its value grew with time, patience, and the ability to keep it alive.
For Leon, those were advantages rather than weaknesses.
The rest of the day passed in controlled urgency.

Shen Baoyuan began moving the most vulnerable warehouse records. Yanning sent messengers to trusted factors without telling any one of them the full reason. Formation workers from another ward arrived through the front gate under the excuse of repairing damage from an old settling crack.
By late afternoon, the estate looked calm from the street and remained tense within its walls.
The outer formation sounded a low warning note.
Every guard in the western yard reached for a weapon.
Leon sensed the approaching presence before the note finished. It crossed the third ward openly, making no attempt to conceal its strength.
He recognized it.
"Stand down," he told the nearest guards. "She is not with Ninefold Ridge."
Yanning joined him as the main gate opened.

Qingyue stepped into the estate with travel dust along the hem of her robe and a shallow, half-healed cut across one forearm. She looked tired, but her steps remained steady. Her gaze moved over the repaired formations, the altered guard posts, and the servants avoiding the rear passage.
Then she looked at Leon.
"Good," Qingyue said. "You waited."
"I completed the investigation in the south," Qingyue said before anyone could ask. "My report has reached the Palace. There is nothing more I need to do there."
