chapters.title: Chapter 628: A Path That Keeps No Element
paragraphs: The circulation became easier with repetition. By the second day he could complete one without concentrating. By the fourth he could run four in succession. By the end of the fifth day the thread had thickened from something like lamplight to something like a candle, which was still absurd and no longer felt absurd.
Then he started putting affinities through it.
Fire went first, because he understood Fire as well as he understood breathing. He drew a thread, gave it fire nature at the intake, and sent it around.
It worked on the first attempt. The route carried it, the neutral section handled it without complaint, and the whole circulation closed clean.
Leon sat with that for a moment, pleased, and then ran Water immediately afterward to confirm.
Water made it to the neutral section and came apart.

It was not violent — the thread destabilized, boiled off, and dispersed harmlessly — but he felt exactly where it happened, and when he examined the route afterward he found what he should have expected.
The fire’s still in there.

Not much of it. A trace, a warmth in the walls of the central section, the beginning of the thing every complete method in the library did deliberately. The route had carried Fire once and had started, immediately, to become a fire route.
So durability wasn’t the problem. Ownership is.
He spent five days on that, and it was the hardest single problem of the month.

What he arrived at eventually was a change to the return path. Instead of letting the energy exit and leave its character behind in the walls, the return section drew the affinity out with it — stripping the elemental influence back into the thread on the way through, so that what left the route took everything it had brought.

It took thirty-one attempts to make that work at all and another forty to make it work reliably. He kept every one of them small. Twice the System flagged accumulating strain in a junction and he stopped for the day, instead of ignoring it because he knew he could heal the damage.
On the twentieth day of the month, Fire went around, and then Water went around behind it, and both completed.
The other affinities each broke it in a new way.

Lightning did not care about the neutral section at all and failed at the transitions instead — it wanted to arrive everywhere at once, and every junction in the route was a place where energy had to change direction. Leon spent two days redesigning four junctions with gentler curves.

Ice slowed. Wherever it passed, the circulation ran thicker and heavier, and a route that ran too slowly in one section and normally in another began to fight itself. A compensating segment cost him another day.

Light and Darkness were the pair he had expected trouble from and the trouble was not what he expected. Neither one damaged the route. They simply refused to enter it while the other’s trace remained — Darkness would not pass through a section that Light had used within the last few minutes, and the reverse was equally true. Once the return-path stripping worked properly, they stopped caring.
Space nearly beat him.

Space left no residue whatsoever, which he took as good news for one entire afternoon before he understood what it was doing instead. It did not change the route’s nature. It changed the route’sposition— bending the geometry of the circulation slightly as it passed, so that the neutral section afterward was in a marginally different place than it had been before. Twice.
The third time he ran it, the return path no longer met the intake.
[Structural deviation: 0.4%]Cumulative deviation across 3 circulations: 1.1%

The System could tell him the number. It could not tell him what to do about it, and Leon spent five days on the answer. He stopped trying to make the route rigid and rebuilt the central section to accept temporary deformation, giving it a resting shape it could return to afterward.
That change turned out to solve two other problems he had been working around.

Ji watched several of the more dangerous tests from her place by the wall. She said very little. But she came to the chamber more often as the weeks went on, and on the day the Space deviation problem resolved she stayed for two hours and left without commenting, which Leon had learned to read.
She’s not here out of obligation anymore.
The disciple registers updated in the third week, and Jade Moon Palace found out about him.

Not much. The aptitude result stayed sealed and the bells stayed unexplained. What went into the public register was three lines: name, age twenty-two, personal disciple of the Palace Mistress — and an assessed cultivation of Peak Golden Core.
That last line did the damage.

Within four days it had reached every core and personal disciple on the mountain, and because the interesting parts were sealed, the explanations invented themselves. Some said he was the heir of a hidden family and Ji had accepted him to secure an alliance. Some said the Palace had struck a bargain with something in the Marches. Some said the assessment was deliberately false, which was closer than the rest and got less traction than any of them.

And on the fifth day, on a training terrace on the eastern side of the mountain, a young man in white and silver-grey listened to a friend read the register aloud and did not say anything for some time.

Wei Zhaoran was ninety-one years old, which for a personal disciple made him young. He had been a Peak Earth Immortal for six years. He had been born with a Lunar Sword Body, a constitution the Palace had recorded eleven times in its history, and he held one of Jade Moon’s forbidden moon techniques by his master’s authority. He had never lost a match against anyone at his own realm, and there were perhaps four people in his generation across the eastern islands who could claim as much.
None of that was a rumor. He had earned every part of it.

Eight years ago, before entering his present master’s lineage, he had asked to be taken as Ji Liansu’s personal disciple and been refused. His Supreme Elder ancestor had formally accepted him soon afterward. Wei had spent the years since explaining to himself that the Palace Mistress simply did not take disciples. It had been a good explanation. He had built quite a lot on top of it.
"Peak Golden Core," he said.
"That’s what it says."
"Read it again."
His friend read it again.
Wei Zhaoran looked out over the terrace toward the sea for a while, and when he spoke his voice was perfectly pleasant.

"She’ll have had a reason," he said. "Everyone has a reason. The question is whether it survives being looked at." He picked up his sword and turned back toward the practice ground. "He’ll have to come out eventually. There’s a gathering at the end of the month."
By the last days of the month, every one of the nine had run the route alone without permanently changing it.
One test remained, and it was the one the whole design existed for.

Not passing Fire through, and then later passing Water through. Going directly from one to the other — inside a single unbroken circulation, without stopping, without letting the route rest, without rebuilding anything in between.
If the neutral section truly owned nothing, that would work.
If it did not, he would find out in the most expensive way available.

chapters.title: Chapter 629: The Formless Myriad Scripture
paragraphs: Ji Liansu came to the chamber at dawn on the thirty-first day.
"You are early," she said. "You have two months remaining."
"I know."
"Then either you have something, or you are about to waste a morning." She took her place by the wall. "Begin."
Leon began with the empty route.

He drew the thread, ran it once around, and let her look. The neutral section took the energy and gave it back exactly as it had received it, and the circulation closed, and nothing anywhere in the room changed.
Then he ran the nine.

Fire, and out. Water, and out. Earth ran heavy and slow and completed. Wind ran fast and completed. Lightning went through the redesigned junctions without touching them. Ice thickened the second stretch and cleared. Light. Darkness. Space, which bent the route by four tenths of a percent and let it come back.
Nine circulations. Nine clean returns. Afterward Leon held the route open and let Ji examine it, and she did, for a long time.
"It has no character," she said.
"That’s the idea."
"Yes." She stepped back. "Do the difficult one."
Leon closed his eyes and started a circulation with Fire at the intake.

He let it get as far as the trunk. Then, without stopping the flow, he changed what he was feeding in — and Water entered the route behind Fire in one continuous stream, with no gap, no pause, and nothing in between them but the neutral section.
He felt them meet.

They did not collide. The Fire ahead reached the return path and was stripped cleanly from the route while the Water followed behind it. By the time Water entered the central section, Fire had left nothing in the walls for it to react against. The same unbroken circulation carried both affinities and returned to neutrality when they were gone.

Light to Darkness was harder. The central section came under real pressure at the transition — he felt it flex, and for a moment he thought it would tear — and then the resting shape reasserted itself and both halves completed.

Space he saved for last, and ran it directly out of Darkness, which was the worst combination he had. The route bent. It bent further than he liked. Then the energy left, and the structure came back to where it had started, and the deviation read zero.
Leon opened his eyes.

Forty-six percent of it, on average, had been going nowhere.
I’ve been paying double for everything I’ve ever done.
He thought about four hours in a bowl of pale stone with a Moonless circling him, and about the garden, and about how much of that fight he had spent on waste he had not known he was producing.
And I’d have lasted nearly twice as long in all of it.

"You will not hit harder," Ji said, watching the pillars. "Understand the actual gift. You can hold the same output for nearly twice as long. You lose very little during circulation now instead of wasting almost half of everything you release. Your control improves because the energy no longer resists you at the moment you use it. And in a long engagement, you will now degrade at roughly the rate your opponent expects a proper cultivator to degrade." She turned. "Also, each circulation will temper your pathways a little. That accumulates over years, and you will not feel it happening."
She paused.
"How you accomplished what you did in the Marches while wasting half your power, I do not want explained. I have decided that it is better for my peace of mind not to know."
Qingyue arrived that afternoon and did not come inside.

"The monthly gathering is in four days," she said from the gate. "Core disciples, personal disciples, and the supervising elders. Announcements, allocations, mission reports, recognitions. As the Palace Mistress’s personal disciple you are expected, and everyone has noticed that you have been in seclusion for a month."
"Then I’ll go."
"Wait." She came a few steps into the yard. "You should know what you are walking into. The register went public three weeks ago. Your age, your position, and Peak Golden Core."
"I assumed it would."
"The mountain has spent three weeks inventing reasons, and none of the reasons are flattering." She folded her arms. "Wei Zhaoran will be there. Do you know the name?"
"No."

"Peak Earth Immortal. Ninety-one. Lunar Sword Body, one of the recorded ones. He holds a moon technique that three people in this Palace are permitted to learn." She said it flatly. "He has never lost to anyone at his own realm, and he earned all of it, which is what makes him difficult. Eight years ago, before entering his present master’s lineage, he asked to become your master’s personal disciple and was refused. He has spent those eight years believing she takes no disciples at all."
"And now she does."

"And now she has taken a twenty-two-year-old at Peak Golden Core." Qingyue met his eyes. "He is not a fool and he will not do anything crude. He believes the appointment is a mistake, and he believes a mistake can be corrected by demonstrating it in public."
Leon thought about the sensible option, which was to stay on this peak and work on the second stage for a year.
"I’m not going to hide up here from an offended swordsman," he said.
"No," Qingyue agreed. "I thought not. Granduncle."

The robes had been waiting in the residence since the day he arrived: pale green over silver-grey, cut close, with the Palace Mistress’s mark at the collar and nothing else anywhere on them. He put them on for the first time and found they fit exactly, which meant someone had measured him at some point without his noticing.
Then he walked out through the compound gate, in daylight, for the first time in a month.

chapters.title: Chapter 630: The Disciple Who Should Have Been Chosen
paragraphs: The gathering was held on the great terrace below the central peak, under an open sky, with the sea running out green and endless to the east.

It was a working assembly. An elder read the season’s allocations — cultivation ground rotations, medicine court quotas, priority on the practice waters. Three mission teams reported: an escort that had gone well, a reef survey that had gone badly, and a beast-clearance in the southern shallows that had cost two outer disciples their lives and produced a long, uncomfortable silence. Four disciples were recognized for advancement, and one was publicly reprimanded over a requisition.
Perhaps three hundred people stood on that terrace, and Leon estimated a hundred and eighty of them looked at him at least once before the announcements finished.
The reactions varied more than Qingyue had implied.

A dozen disciples greeted him with genuine courtesy, because the Palace Mistress had chosen him and that was sufficient. Many more simply stared at a face that had produced three weeks of rumor. A group near the eastern rail was openly unimpressed, and one of them said something that made the others laugh quietly, none of them looking at him while they did it.
Qingyue stood beside him through the announcements and said nothing on his behalf.

When an elder called his name for formal acknowledgment as the Palace Mistress’s personal disciple, she stepped back half a pace and bowed with everyone else, and afterward, in front of perhaps forty people, she said, "This way, Granduncle," and the resulting ripple ran halfway across the terrace.
"You enjoyed that," Leon said.
"I did not. It is protocol." A pause. "It was slightly satisfying."
Wei Zhaoran came over as the assembly began to loosen.
He was tall and unhurried, in white and silver-grey with a plain sword at his hip, and the crowd opened for him without appearing to. He stopped at a courteous distance and bowed a courteous amount.
"Junior Brother Leon," he said. "Wei Zhaoran. Welcome to Jade Moon Palace — belatedly, since I understand you have been in seclusion since the day you arrived."
"A month of it."

"Productive, I hope." His tone was warm and entirely pleasant. "There is a great deal here worth a month. May I ask what you were studying? The library sees a great many new disciples and very few of them for thirty-one days without emerging."
"Circulation theory, mostly."

"Ah." Wei nodded slowly. "Foundational work. There is no shame in it." He turned slightly, so his voice carried to the twenty or so people who had gathered near without appearing to gather. "You will find the Palace generous. I would offer one thought, since nobody else is likely to say it to you directly and I would rather it came from someone who means you no harm."
"Go on."

"A personal disciple does not stand for himself." Wei’s manner remained perfectly even. "When I walk into a hall in the outer islands, people do not see Wei Zhaoran. They see my master’s judgment. Every match I have fought since entering her lineage has been a report on her." He gestured lightly at the terrace. "The Palace Mistress has taken no personal disciple in a very long time. Whoever she chose was always going to be looked at closely, by us and by everyone outside these islands who hears about it."
"That seems reasonable."

"I hoped you would think so. Which is why I would rather ask honestly than let the question circulate as gossip." Wei’s eyes came up. "The register lists your cultivation as Peak Golden Core. Every personal disciple on this terrace is in the immortal realms. When the eastern sects send representatives at the turn of the year and ask who speaks for the Palace Mistress’s lineage — what shall we tell them?"
There it was.

The crowd had grown considerably. Leon could feel the shape of what Wei wanted: irritation, or a boast, or a hint about the sealed record, or the flustered silence of a young man asked a fair question in public with no good answer.
"Tell them what’s in the register," Leon said. "It’s accurate."
Wei waited for more and did not get any.
"That is all?"

"My master knew my cultivation when she accepted me. She had the record in her hand." Leon’s tone did not change. "If her judgment needs defending, she’s better placed to defend it than I am. And if the eastern sects want to form an opinion about a line in a register, I don’t think anything I say here changes it."
Something behind Wei’s pleasantness shifted.
"That is a very composed answer," he said.
"It’s the true one."

"Then let me be less composed, since we have both been polite long enough." Wei’s voice stayed level and stopped being warm. "Eight years ago I asked the Palace Mistress to take me as her personal disciple. I was refused, and I accepted it, because I told myself she took no disciples. I then spent eight years becoming the strongest disciple of my generation on these islands. That is a record anyone here may check, not a claim."
Nobody on the terrace was pretending to talk about anything else now.

"Then she accepted you," Wei said. "In one morning. Without a trial, without a service record, without a single day of contribution to this Palace. A stranger from the frontier at Peak Golden Core." He drew a breath. "I do not think you are a liar and I do not think you are a fraud. I think a mistake has been made, and I think the only honest way to establish that is to find out what you can actually do."
He stepped back one pace and bowed properly, formally, from the waist.
"I request a spar with Junior Brother Leon. Before the assembly, under an elder’s supervision."
The terrace erupted.

It was arithmetic more than outrage on Leon’s behalf. Someone saidPeak Earth Immortalloudly enough to carry. An elder near the front called out that a Peak Golden Core disciple could not be asked to face one in any format whatsoever, three other voices agreed, and one added that Wei knew it perfectly well.
Wei let it run for exactly as long as it took to become general.

"Of course," he said, and the terrace quieted. "I would not insult anyone by proposing that. I will seal my cultivation to Peak Golden Core for the duration and hold it there. Publicly, before I enter, so that every person here can verify it."
He turned back to Leon.

"At equal cultivation," he said, "nothing decides the outcome except foundation, control, experience, and technique. Those are the only things I have ever claimed. If yours are better than mine, then the Palace Mistress was right and I was wrong, and I will say so where everyone can hear it."
And if I refuse, that’s an answer too.
Leon looked past him.

Ji Liansu had come onto the terrace at some point, and he had no idea when. She stood at the top of the steps with her hands folded inside her sleeves, and she had clearly heard everything, and she said nothing at all.
She waited until he looked at her.
"Do you wish to accept?" she asked.

That was all. No warning, no permission, no assessment of the odds. She had left the entire decision on the terrace where it belonged, and Leon understood that she would have supported a refusal just as calmly.
"I do," he said.
Only then did Ji Liansu come down the steps.

"Then it is a supervised match," she said, and her voice reached the whole terrace without effort. "No deliberate killing. Neither participant may use an external treasure whose grade exceeds the declared level of the duel. It ends by surrender, by incapacity, or when the supervising elder calls it." She looked at Wei. "You will seal in the open where the assembly can see it, and you will hold that seal for the full match."
"Of course, Palace Mistress."
The arena stood on the lower terrace already — a sunken circle sixty paces across with barrier pillars at eight points. Three hundred people moved toward it without anyone giving an instruction.

Wei went to the center and did exactly as he had promised. He drew his cultivation down in front of all of them, layer by layer, and Leon watched something enormous fold itself smaller and smaller until what remained standing in the circle read as an ordinary, solid, unremarkable Peak Golden Core.
He rolled his shoulders once and looked entirely at ease.
Leon stepped down into the circle across from him, in pale green and silver-grey, carrying no weapon and nothing anyone could see.
First real test.
He had eight familiar techniques and half the fuel cost he used to pay for them, and he had never once used the Formless Myriad Scripture in a fight.
The barrier pillars lit, and the wall came up around them, and the noise of the terrace cut out.

chapters.title: Chapter 631: The Moon Meets the Myriad
paragraphs: The barrier closed, and the terrace fell silent.
Inside the circle, the sea became a distant murmur. Formation pillars hummed around the arena, and a cold current gathered where none had existed a moment earlier.

Wei Zhaoran stood forty paces away with his sword still sheathed. His cultivation remained exactly where he had placed it before the gathered disciples—Peak Golden Core, steady and without the slightest fluctuation. Whatever else could be said about him, he had kept his word about the restriction.
And he is still dangerous.

Leon saw it in his stance. Wei’s breathing had slowed, and the pale current surrounding him gathered along his arms and the line of his sheath. There was no wasted tension in his body. At ninety-one, he had never lost to anyone at his own realm, and that reputation had not been built on pride alone.
Good.

Leon had no interest in humiliating him. Thirty-one days of solitary practice had given the Formless Myriad Scripture a stable first stage, but every test had taken place inside a sealed chamber. Meditation could not show him what the neutral circulation route would do when another cultivator was trying to cut him apart.

He started the Scripture and allowed ordinary mana to flow through its central route. The Primordial Void Heart remained quiet. He did not touch the Divinordial Heart at all. Its holy energy had no place in a mana-based duel, and forcing the two energies together would create more danger than Wei’s sword.
Wei drew.
The slash was already finished when Leon moved. The blade passed through the place his shoulder had occupied and left a crescent of pale light hanging in the air.
Leon watched it for half a heartbeat.
Wei stepped left and cut again. His second stroke came nowhere near Leon, but the suspended crescent awakened and shot toward Leon’s back from an impossible angle.
Leon folded three inches of space and let it pass beside his ribs.
"Good," Wei said.
He cut twice more.

Wei’s swordsmanship was economical, with every stroke either threatening Leon directly or leaving another crescent behind. Ice spread across the floor, cracking and refreezing under their feet. Moonlight distorted the reach of his blade: attacks that should have required another step arrived early, while strikes that appeared close stopped half a pace short.
Within two minutes, eleven crescents divided the arena into narrowing wedges. Wei was not chasing Leon. He was steadily removing every safe place Leon might use.
Leon answered with two affinities.

Space shortened his steps and shifted his body a few degrees at a time. Lightning remained inside his muscles, sharpening his acceleration without wasting mana on visible bolts. He avoided the crescents instead of destroying them and watched how Wei connected one sequence to the next.
Wei soon began freezing the ground ahead of Leon, predicting his spatial steps and taking away his footing.
Leon added Ice.
Rather than shatter the frozen surface, he seized control of it. His next three steps crossed ice that now answered him instead of Wei, and the crescent timed to catch his stumble struck empty air.
A murmur rose beyond the barrier.

Light came next. Wei placed his crescents edge-on inside blind angles, so Leon spread a thin glow across the arena and exposed their outlines. Darkness followed when reflected moonlight began multiplying across the ice and barrier. It swallowed the false images, leaving only the real blade and the crescents attached to it.

Leon introduced each affinity gradually. By the time all five moved through the same central route, the watching disciples had understood that this was not a sequence of separate techniques. A Peak Golden Core cultivator was circulating five affinities together.
Wei understood something else.

The first time he used a delayed-crescent bind, Leon needed four exchanges to escape it. The second time required two. On the third attempt, Leon was gone before the formation closed. When Wei tried it again, Leon allowed three crescents to converge, then stepped through a fold in space a fraction before they struck each other.
Wei’s expression hardened. Leon had not been struggling through his prepared sequences. He had been learning them.
Even so, Wei remained dangerous.

His Lunar Sword Body carried intent through muscle, bone, and blade with almost no waste. His control of the arena forced Leon to attempt affinity transitions faster than the unfinished Scripture could safely manage.

Wei also adapted once he understood Leon’s purpose. He stopped repeating complete sequences and began breaking them apart midway, turning a familiar bind into an immediate thrust or awakening a crescent earlier than its established rhythm allowed. One feint made Leon fold space toward what appeared to be the only opening, only for moonlight to shorten Wei’s next cut and meet him there. Leon twisted away, but the blade shaved ice from his shoulder and forced him to abandon the step.

That exchange changed the value of the practice. Wei was no longer displaying techniques for Leon to solve. He was watching Leon’s solutions and building traps for them. The Scripture now had to survive an opponent who understood that it was being tested.
At the eleventh minute, Leon moved directly from Lightning into Ice.
The two currents collided inside the trunk of the circulation route. Pain tore through his chest, and his footing slowed for less than a second.
Wei found the opening.
A crescent passed through Leon’s guard and cut his left side from hip to ribs. Blood darkened his robe as he retreated two steps.
Lightning cannot enter Ice directly at this speed. The neutral section needs time to settle.
Leon inserted a single beat into the transition and ran it again. This time, the route held.
The wound was real, but so was the answer it had purchased.
Leon stopped retreating.

He began dismantling the crescents before they activated. Light exposed an edge, Darkness severed the reflection feeding it, and a thread of Lightning broke its timing. Four crescents vanished in quick succession. Wei formed three more, and Leon destroyed two while advancing.
The audience saw the change. Wei was still attacking, but the space he controlled was shrinking around him.

Wei tried to rebuild the formation twice. Leon denied him both times, first by freezing the point where a crescent needed to anchor and then by folding its reflected partner into the same space. The two constructs struck each other and vanished. Wei’s next attack came without preparation, a clean sword thrust reinforced by his Lunar Sword Body, and Leon had to meet it directly. Their mana collided hard enough to fracture the ice beneath them.
Leon put Lightning into a spatial step and crossed the arena through the narrowest gap in the sword formation. Wei’s blade turned toward him at once.
Leon caught the flat with an ice-sheathed palm, smothered the moonlight along its edge with Darkness, and pushed.
Wei slid backward three steps.
For the first time since the duel began, surprise broke through his composure. Leon had reached him while testing an unfinished cultivation technique, and the gap between them was still growing.
Wei tightened both hands around his sword and drew the moon art inward, plainly attempting to keep it contained within the seal and end the duel cleanly.
Silver-blue light gathered beneath the barrier. A false moon began forming above the arena, enormous and cold enough to thicken the ice across the floor.
Then the technique touched Wei’s Lunar Sword Body.
The two resonated.
Wei’s face changed. He tried to stop, but the art fed his body, and his body returned more power to the art. Hairline fractures of light spread through the suppression seal beneath his ribs.
"No," Wei said.
The first crack opened.
Power far beyond Peak Golden Core descended over the arena.

chapters.title: Chapter 632: To Unmake a False Moon
paragraphs: The suppression seal failed in stages.

Wei fought it with both hands locked around his sword, but the false moon had already connected to his Lunar Sword Body. The art pulled power from him, his body amplified it, and the seal stood between two forces that were no longer listening to their owner.
If Wei stopped now, the gathered lunar energy would collapse into his own channels.
The second crack opened, followed by a third. Then the suppression came apart, releasing Wei’s true cultivation in three heavy waves.
[Wei Zhaoran — Mid Void Immortal]
Mid Ethereal Initiate.
The arena barrier groaned.

Ji Liansu moved immediately. A pale curtain rose outside the original barrier, separating the arena from the terrace, while two elders drove their authority into the formation pillars. Another elder ordered the nearest rows back. The disciples retreated without argument as the second barrier hardened between them and the false moon.
Leon caught Ji Liansu’s gaze through the layered formations. Her hand was raised, ready to pull him out.

The lunar art had wound itself through the original barrier. Its light ran down the pillars and into the containment formation, using the arena as part of its own structure. Tearing Leon out would save him, but it would not save Wei or prevent the trapped lunar power from detonating.
Leon shook his head once.
Ji Liansu’s expression did not change. The outer barrier brightened until the retreating disciples were protected, but she allowed Leon several more breaths to act.
He had wanted a real test for the Scripture. That no longer mattered. The false moon had to be dismantled from inside before it destroyed Wei and the arena with him.
The advantage Leon had built disappeared.

Wei’s sword did not merely become faster. Inside the false moon’s territory, every reflection became a place from which a sword might emerge. Ice formed in the air as suspended sheets, turning and catching silver light. Moonlight distorted distance until attacks arrived from positions Wei’s body had never occupied.
Space saved Leon from the first three strikes.
The fourth opened his shoulder. The fifth tore through his defense and drove him across the frozen arena.

Leon regained his footing and circulated more mana. The unfinished route protested at once. Every affinity now passed through it at a volume it had never been designed to carry. One junction tore in his upper chest, then another beneath it. Blood entered his mouth, and his breathing grew heavy.
[Circulation strain: severe]
[Junction damage: 3 confirmed]
I know.

At equal cultivation, Leon’s body, affinities, and foundation had placed him far above Wei’s expectations. None of that erased the difference between Peak Golden Core and Mid Void Immortal. Wei was also a genius whose strength surpassed his nominal realm. For several exchanges, neither could gain a decisive advantage: Wei’s territory and swordsmanship prevented Leon from advancing, while Leon’s body and Space affinity denied Wei a killing blow.
The stalemate was already costing Leon more.

Wei drove him toward the western pillar with a sequence that no longer depended on delayed crescents. Three reflected blades attacked from separate angles while the real sword remained held at Wei’s side. Leon folded away from the first, blocked the second with Ice, and let the third scrape across his ribs because defending it would have exposed his throat. Wei’s actual blade arrived through the flash of pain.

Leon caught the edge between two spatial layers. The impact still forced him to one knee. He released the trapped sword before the layers collapsed and rolled beneath a sheet of airborne ice as it snapped shut where his head had been.

Wei gave him no pause. That relentless control was what separated him from the Void Immortals Leon had killed before. Those cultivators had possessed higher realms. Wei knew how to make every fragment of his realm matter.
He opened the Primordial Void Heart.

No light appeared, and his aura did not change. The lunar mana penetrating his defenses simply stopped accumulating inside him. The Heart separated the unstable portions, refined what it could, and returned a fraction to his circulation as usable mana.
It did not make him immune to Wei’s art. It gave him enough time to solve it.

Leon had continued switching affinities as he always had: Lightning for speed, Ice for stability, Space for movement. Each transition forced one current out before the next could enter, and the repeated changes were tearing the incomplete route apart.
So he stopped switching.
He opened the neutral center and brought all five affinities into one continuous circulation.

Pain ripped through his channels. For an instant, the competing currents threatened to tear the route open from within. Ice stabilized the flow first. Lightning moved inside it, providing speed without entering as a separate surge. Light spread through the territory and mapped the false moon’s reflections. Darkness erased the paths that existed only as illusions. Space showed him which distances were real.
The currents settled.
For eleven breaths, the false moon stopped looking like an overwhelming domain. Leon could see how it worked.

Every reflected sword drew power from another. Destroying one allowed the moon to rebuild it through the next connection, but each connection possessed a junction. Leon had spent the last month learning how junctions failed.
He advanced.

Darkness swallowed the first reflection. Light exposed the connection behind it, and Lightning broke the timing before the false moon could refill the gap. Ice caught the released lunar mana and prevented it from exploding. Space redirected the collapse toward the empty center of the arena.
Leon repeated the sequence.

Silver fragments separated from the false moon and dissolved while falling. More junctions appeared as the territory weakened, and Leon broke them without allowing the cycle to repair itself. From beyond the reinforced barriers, it looked as though he were peeling the moon apart one piece at a time.
Wei felt the technique collapsing. His eyes no longer tracked Leon properly, and the forbidden art drove him toward the only conclusion it still understood.
He gathered everything into a final sword strike.
Leon crossed the remaining distance through Space. He arrived inside the arc of the blade, caught its flat with one palm, and placed his other hand against Wei’s chest.
Then he severed the final connection between Wei and the false moon.
The domain collapsed.
Every reflection vanished, the frost began receding from the barrier, and Wei’s sword rang against the stone. For one breath, he remained standing.
Then the backlash reversed through his channels.
Wei’s knees gave way. Leon caught him before he hit the ground.

Through the contact between them, the Primordial Void Heart drew out the lunar energy tearing through Wei’s meridians. It could not undo every injury, but it removed enough unstable power to prevent the backlash from reaching his foundation.
The watching disciples saw Leon stabilize a defeated opponent with extraordinary mana control. Neither they nor the elders detected the Heart itself.

The last pieces of the false moon dissolved above the ruined arena. Leon remained standing despite the blood covering his side and the damage inside his channels, supporting the man who had nearly killed him.
A Supreme Elder descended through the outer barrier.
He went to Wei first.
Leon expected nothing else.

chapters.title: Chapter 633: A Debt Beneath the Moon
paragraphs: The Supreme Elder knelt beside Wei and placed two fingers against his throat.
Leon lowered Wei onto the stone and stepped back. The arena remained silent while the old man examined his descendant’s channels and foundation.
After nearly a minute, he rose.

"The lunar energy has been removed from his channels," he announced. His voice crossed both barriers without effort. "His meridians are damaged, but they will heal. His foundation is intact, and he will keep his cultivation."
Relief passed through several disciples on the terrace.
The Supreme Elder turned toward them rather than Leon.

"This duel was agreed at Peak Golden Core. Wei Zhaoran exceeded that restriction. I do not believe he broke it intentionally, but intention does not change the result. He invoked a technique he could not control, and the breach was his."
His gaze moved across the gathering.

"Leon won the duel they agreed to. When the restriction failed, he survived Wei’s full cultivation, destroyed the forbidden art, and saved Wei’s foundation afterward. There will be no dispute over the result."
No one challenged him.
Only then did he face Leon.
"You could have stepped aside after the moon art collapsed," the elder said. "No one would have blamed you for allowing the backlash to take its course."
"He wasn’t in control by then."

"No, he was not." The Supreme Elder glanced down at Wei. "I allowed a descendant to inherit a technique he had the talent to invoke but not the discipline to hold. His punishment will be handled within my line, but the greater failure began with me."
He bowed.
It was a restrained gesture, yet a bow from a Supreme Elder to a new personal disciple carried more weight than any public speech.
"My line owes you Wei’s life and foundation," he said. "That debt will not be ignored. We will speak again after he wakes and I have finished being angry with him."
He lifted Wei and left the arena.

The gathering did not dissolve into admiration. Leon preferred that. Some disciples watched him with open respect, others with envy or disbelief. Several were clearly reconsidering every rumor they had heard about Ji Liansu’s new disciple.

Fresh rumors began before the terrace emptied. Some credited an ancient constitution. Others assumed Ji Liansu had given Leon a lost inheritance during his month of seclusion. A formation disciple argued that the five-affinity circulation had not resembled anything stored in the Palace library and might have been created by Leon himself.
That explanation received the least support despite being closest to the truth.

Ji Liansu entered the arena after the last disciples had withdrawn. She did not congratulate Leon. She placed two fingers over the mana route near his sternum and followed the residue left by the damaged circulation. Leon kept both Hearts dormant while she examined only the pathways used by the Formless Myriad Scripture.
"Four damaged junctions," she said.
"Three."

"You have not found the fourth yet. You will tomorrow." She withdrew her hand. "The first stage maintained five affinities under the pressure of a Mid Void Immortal’s forbidden art. The central principle is viable."
"That sounds almost approving."

"Then listen carefully to the rest." Ji Liansu’s voice remained calm. "You forced power through channels that have not finished adapting to one affinity, much less five. Another few exchanges would have caused permanent damage. You proved that the Scripture can work. You did not prove that this version is safe."
Leon could not dispute that.

"No experiments until the tearing closes," she continued. "No multi-affinity circulation, and no ordinary circulation until tomorrow at the earliest. If you attempt to bargain, I will make the restriction a month."
"I wasn’t going to bargain."
"Good. Perhaps the duel taught you two useful things."
Recovery required five days.

The fourth damaged junction announced itself the next morning exactly as Ji Liansu predicted. Leon allowed no mana into the Scripture for two full days. At night, after confirming that the mana cycle was completely closed and every formation around his residence was sealed, he used a small amount of holy energy from the Divinordial Heart to support his body’s recovery. The two energies never entered the same channels at the same time.
On the third day, he tested a single thread of neutral mana. On the fourth, he completed one slow circulation without pain.

Most of his time went into reviewing the duel. The Lightning-to-Ice collision could be corrected by giving the neutral center another fraction of time to settle. The deeper damage had come from forcing five affinities through pathways designed to carry one current at a time.

The Primordial Void Heart had also carried too much of the burden. It had processed hostile lunar mana that the Scripture failed to isolate. Leon did not expect the Scripture to imitate the Heart’s unique assimilation ability, but its next stage needed to protect its circulation from foreign energy and coordinate multiple affinities without relying on the Heart as a constant safety net.
He recorded both requirements and set them aside until Ji Liansu’s restriction ended.
Wei visited on the fifth day with another elder waiting outside the courtyard.
He was pale and moved carefully, but he remained on his feet. He stopped before Leon and bowed lower than their difference in status required.
"I broke the restriction," Wei said. "The moon art overwhelmed the seal, but that does not excuse invoking it. I brought a technique I could not control into an agreed duel. The fault is mine."
"All right."
Wei’s jaw tightened, perhaps because Leon had made accepting the apology harder by refusing to argue.
"You also saved my life and foundation," he continued. "You had already forced me back before the seal failed. No one from my line will claim the outcome was unclear."
Leon studied him for a moment.
"Your swordsmanship was a genuine problem," he said. "The delayed crescents nearly ended the duel twice. I took that wound because you forced me into a transition the Scripture wasn’t ready to make."
Wei raised his head. Some of the strain left his face.
"That is kinder than I deserve."
"It is accurate. Being dangerous and losing are not mutually exclusive."
Wei accepted that with a small nod. "I will challenge you again, but not soon. The next time, it will be with power I can control and skill I have earned since this defeat."
"Then I will look forward to it." Leon paused. "Try to arrange matters so I don’t have to save you afterward. It is an inconvenient way to end a duel."
Wei almost smiled. He bowed once more and left.

That evening, Leon sat beneath the plum tree in his courtyard and considered the time that had passed. He had originally promised the four women nearly three outside months to adapt to the local cultivation system. Barely more than one month had passed for him, but it had become more than ten months inside the dimensional world.
They were not supposed to be ready yet.
After what he had learned about cultivation methods refusing to follow expectations, Leon no longer trusted the schedule more than the result.
He checked the residence formations, entered the sealed hall, and opened the path home.

sentences.text: The Supreme Elder knelt beside Wei and placed two fingers against his throat.
Leon lowered Wei onto the stone and stepped back.
The arena remained silent while the old man examined his descendant’s channels and foundation.
After nearly a minute, he rose.
"The lunar energy has been removed from his channels," he announced.
His voice crossed both barriers without effort.
"His meridians are damaged, but they will heal.
His foundation is intact, and he will keep his cultivation."
Relief passed through several disciples on the terrace.
The Supreme Elder turned toward them rather than Leon.
"This duel was agreed at Peak Golden Core.
Wei Zhaoran exceeded that restriction.
I do not believe he broke it intentionally, but intention does not change the result.
He invoked a technique he could not control, and the breach was his."
His gaze moved across the gathering.
"Leon won the duel they agreed to.
When the restriction failed, he survived Wei’s full cultivation, destroyed the forbidden art, and saved Wei’s foundation afterward.
There will be no dispute over the result."
No one challenged him.
Only then did he face Leon.
"You could have stepped aside after the moon art collapsed," the elder said.
"No one would have blamed you for allowing the backlash to take its course."
"He wasn’t in control by then."
"No, he was not." The Supreme Elder glanced down at Wei.
"I allowed a descendant to inherit a technique he had the talent to invoke but not the discipline to hold.
His punishment will be handled within my line, but the greater failure began with me."
He bowed.
It was a restrained gesture, yet a bow from a Supreme Elder to a new personal disciple carried more weight than any public speech.
"My line owes you Wei’s life and foundation," he said.
"That debt will not be ignored.
We will speak again after he wakes and I have finished being angry with him."
He lifted Wei and left the arena.
The gathering did not dissolve into admiration.
Leon preferred that.
Some disciples watched him with open respect, others with envy or disbelief.
Several were clearly reconsidering every rumor they had heard about Ji Liansu’s new disciple.
Fresh rumors began before the terrace emptied.
Some credited an ancient constitution.
Others assumed Ji Liansu had given Leon a lost inheritance during his month of seclusion.
A formation disciple argued that the five-affinity circulation had not resembled anything stored in the Palace library and might have been created by Leon himself.
That explanation received the least support despite being closest to the truth.
Ji Liansu entered the arena after the last disciples had withdrawn.
She did not congratulate Leon.
She placed two fingers over the mana route near his sternum and followed the residue left by the damaged circulation.
Leon kept both Hearts dormant while she examined only the pathways used by the Formless Myriad Scripture.
"Four damaged junctions," she said.
"Three."
"You have not found the fourth yet.
You will tomorrow." She withdrew her hand.
"The first stage maintained five affinities under the pressure of a Mid Void Immortal’s forbidden art.
The central principle is viable."
"That sounds almost approving."
"Then listen carefully to the rest." Ji Liansu’s voice remained calm.
"You forced power through channels that have not finished adapting to one affinity, much less five.
Another few exchanges would have caused permanent damage.
You proved that the Scripture can work.
You did not prove that this version is safe."
Leon could not dispute that.
"No experiments until the tearing closes," she continued.
"No multi-affinity circulation, and no ordinary circulation until tomorrow at the earliest.
If you attempt to bargain, I will make the restriction a month."
"I wasn’t going to bargain."
"Good.
Perhaps the duel taught you two useful things."
Recovery required five days.
The fourth damaged junction announced itself the next morning exactly as Ji Liansu predicted.
Leon allowed no mana into the Scripture for two full days.

At night, after confirming that the mana cycle was completely closed and every formation around his residence was sealed, he used a small amount of holy energy from the Divinordial Heart to support his body’s recovery.
The two energies never entered the same channels at the same time.
On the third day, he tested a single thread of neutral mana.
On the fourth, he completed one slow circulation without pain.
Most of his time went into reviewing the duel.
The Lightning-to-Ice collision could be corrected by giving the neutral center another fraction of time to settle.
The deeper damage had come from forcing five affinities through pathways designed to carry one current at a time.
The Primordial Void Heart had also carried too much of the burden.
It had processed hostile lunar mana that the Scripture failed to isolate.

Leon did not expect the Scripture to imitate the Heart’s unique assimilation ability, but its next stage needed to protect its circulation from foreign energy and coordinate multiple affinities without relying on the Heart as a constant safety net.
He recorded both requirements and set them aside until Ji Liansu’s restriction ended.

He was pale and moved carefully, but he remained on his feet.
He stopped before Leon and bowed lower than their difference in status required.
"I broke the restriction," Wei said.
"The moon art overwhelmed the seal, but that does not excuse invoking it.
I brought a technique I could not control into an agreed duel.
The fault is mine."
"All right."
Wei’s jaw tightened, perhaps because Leon had made accepting the apology harder by refusing to argue.
"You also saved my life and foundation," he continued.
"You had already forced me back before the seal failed.
No one from my line will claim the outcome was unclear."
Leon studied him for a moment.
"Your swordsmanship was a genuine problem," he said.
"The delayed crescents nearly ended the duel twice.
I took that wound because you forced me into a transition the Scripture wasn’t ready to make."

chapters.title: Chapter 634: Ten Months Beyond the Door
paragraphs: Leon emerged into afternoon light and the smell of turned earth.

The contrast disoriented him for a moment. Jade Moon Palace was cold stone, sea wind, and the constant presence of hundreds of cultivators. His dimensional world was warm and familiar. A work bell rang somewhere down the slope, and cultivated fields stretched green beneath a clear sky.
Seraphine crossed the room before he had fully steadied himself.
She caught his collar and began opening his robe.
"It is healed," Leon said.
"That is the second time you have greeted me with that sentence."
Her hands stopped over the faint discoloration along his left side. The original wound had closed, but less than a week had not been enough to erase every trace of the damaged junctions beneath it.
"What happened?" she asked.
"A cultivation route tore during a duel."
"A cultivation route," Seraphine repeated. "You fought someone while using the unfinished technique you told me was unsafe at high volume."
"Yes."
She stared at him for two seconds, then pointed toward a chair.
"Sit down and explain everything. Do not use the voice you use when reporting damaged supplies."
Ira entered from the terrace while Leon was sitting.

"One month," she said, dropping sideways into another chair. "We leave you alone for one month, and you find the strongest personal disciple in the Palace. Did you ask for directions, or did he come looking for you?"
"He challenged me."
"Of course he did. You have a face that encourages poor decisions." Ira looked at Seraphine. "How badly was he hurt?"
"He is about to tell us," Seraphine said, "if no one interrupts him again."

Leon gave them the complete account. He explained Wei’s restriction, the delayed crescents, the affinity transition that failed, and the false moon that shattered the seal. He described the five-affinity circulation and the damage it caused. He also told them that the Primordial Void Heart had processed the lunar mana invading his body, while the Divinordial Heart and its holy energy remained inactive throughout the duel.
Vyra appeared at the window midway through the explanation. She listened with her arms folded and waited until he finished.
"Mid Void Immortal," she said. "Two major realms above the cultivation you displayed."
"Yes."
"And the strongest personal disciple of a major sect, not another hired attacker."
"Also yes."
"Could you defeat him again if he remained clear-headed and used his full cultivation from the beginning?"
Leon considered the question honestly.

"A prolonged fight would be far more difficult. The forbidden art made him stronger, but it also trapped him inside one pattern. I found its structure because he could no longer change it. Against a clear-headed Mid Void Immortal Wei Zhaoran, I would need a different answer."
Vyra nodded. "Good. I wanted to know whether you understood the distinction. What else did the fight teach us about this world?"

"That Jade Moon Palace’s strongest personal disciple reached Mid Void Immortal at ninety-one, and that the elders above him are separated by more than cultivation alone. My master could have ended the danger herself once the spectators were protected. She allowed me the chance to dismantle it because I told her I could."
Loriel had remained quiet. She sat beside Leon and held one hand near his side, her attention sinking beneath the surface.
"There is still strain here," she said softly. "And along the front. The damage is closed, but the channels remember its shape."
"Ji Liansu said it would fade with time."
"She is right." Loriel allowed a gentle current of Life energy to enter him. "I cannot erase it, but I can make the recovery easier."
Leon waited until she looked up.
"It was preventable," he told her. "I promised all of you that I would use safeguards, then accepted a duel while the Scripture was incomplete. You are allowed to be angry."
"I’m not angry."
"That is worse," Ira said.
"I know," Loriel murmured, returning her attention to his side.
Seraphine did not release the matter so easily. "The next time you test it against someone capable of killing you, I expect to know beforehand."
"That is fair."
"I was not negotiating."
Despite her tone, some of the tension left her shoulders.
Leon spent the rest of the afternoon examining what more than ten accelerated months had accomplished.
[Seraphine — Peak Foundation Establishment]
[Ira — Peak Foundation Establishment]
[Vyra — Peak Foundation Establishment]
[Loriel — Peak Foundation Establishment]

All four had formed genuine local foundations. Their personal Classes remained exactly what they had always been: Seraphine was a Stormlight Sword Saint, Ira a Calamity Flame Lancer, Vyra a Pyran Flame Sovereign, and Loriel a Child of Life. Cultivation had not replaced or competed with those paths. It refined the bodies, channels, and energy control supporting them.
Their previous progression had advanced faster than their internal structures could fully accommodate. Peak Foundation Establishment had begun closing that gap.
Leon asked for demonstrations rather than four complete spars.

Seraphine drew her sword and cut once. Stormlight traveled along the blade in a controlled taper instead of flaring outward. Lightning and Light moved together through a foundation built around speed, protection, and precise killing. The strike reached farther than her older attacks while consuming less power.

Ira compressed Fire into a narrow line along her spear and drove it through a prepared slab of stone. The weapon left a clean circular opening instead of exploding the entire slab. The destructive force had not weakened; it had learned where to go.

Vyra’s demonstration was less visible. Her flame settled around her in a deep, steady pressure suited to holding a battlefield and coordinating others. She maintained it without the waste Leon remembered from her earlier power.
Loriel led him to the quarantine plot. The Earthmarrow fern had grown four new fronds, and the soil had darkened for two paces around it.
"Foundation Establishment," Loriel said, sounding embarrassed by her own success. "Stable circulation makes it easier to understand what the plant needs."
"That is not the only reason it grew."
"No," she admitted. "But it helped."
Leon crouched beside the fern and examined the healthy new growth.

He had given them nearly three outside months because he believed they would need more than two years inside to reach a safe stopping point. They had achieved his real objective in less than half that time. Their local cultivation signatures were stable, their foreign energy structures no longer stood exposed, and each could pass naturally as an unusual Foundation Establishment cultivator.
They had done it through months of work he had not witnessed.
Pride came first. Regret followed more quietly. For him, their separation had lasted little more than a month. They had lived almost a year without him.
Seraphine came to stand beside him. "Is something wrong?"
"No. The opposite." Leon rose. "You reached the target far earlier than I expected. There is no reason to keep you here for the rest of the schedule simply because I once guessed you would need it."
Ira leaned on her spear. "Does that mean what I think it means?"
"It means we prepare your identities properly, and then you come with me."
Loriel looked toward the place where the passage usually opened. Vyra was already considering the practical problems. Seraphine only watched Leon, as though waiting to make sure he meant it.
"The waiting is almost over," he said.

chapters.title: Chapter 635: Four Attendants from Nowhere
paragraphs: They began planning that evening.

Leon would not bring four unregistered cultivators directly into his secluded residence. Even if no formation detected the passage, their sudden appearance inside Jade Moon Palace would make every later explanation harder. They needed to enter through the same gate as everyone else and leave a clean record behind them.

"Personal attendants connected to my sealed inheritance," Leon said. "That remains the public truth. You survived the same collapsed secret realm and remained behind while I established myself outside. We will not provide details the Palace has no right to demand."
Vyra sat opposite him with a blank book already open. "Who approves the registration?"
"My direct-disciple token allows me to sponsor attendants, but Ji Liansu’s written approval will prevent lower officials from treating the unusual circumstances as an invitation to investigate."
"Where do we appear?"

"A palace-controlled port outside the sect. I will secure a private courtyard, enter the dimensional world from there, and take all four of you out through the same passage. Then we approach the front gate openly."
Vyra wrote it down. "Better. Our first public sighting cannot be inside the Palace."
"Exactly."

They confirmed their roles next. Seraphine would be registered as Leon’s chief attendant and personal guard. Ira would serve as his combat guard, Vyra as steward and adviser, and Loriel as the attendant responsible for medicinal plants and gardens.

Their Classes required no invented explanation. Classes were personal paths, and this world already possessed countless inheritances, bloodline arts, constitutions, and cultivation variations. Anyone who noticed an unusual quality in their power could reasonably assume it came from the collapsed secret realm. Their Peak Foundation Establishment cultivation would be the part officials could measure and record.
"Who outranks us?" Vyra asked.

"Almost everyone with formal authority," Leon said. "You are attached to me, not disciples of Jade Moon Palace. An elder can issue instructions concerning Palace law, safety, or restricted grounds. They cannot casually transfer your service or command you on private matters without going through me."
"And if a core disciple gives Ira an order?"
"I ignore it politely," Ira answered.
Vyra looked at Leon.
"She declines anything unrelated to Palace rules," Leon said. "Politely."
"That sounds less entertaining," Ira said.
"It is meant to."
Seraphine folded her arms. "Chief attendant means I remain near you."
"Usually."
"Near enough to know before you accept another duel involving an unfinished cultivation technique."
"I already agreed to that."
"I wanted it included in the official duties."
Ira laughed. Even Vyra’s mouth moved slightly before she returned to her notes.
Loriel had been quiet through most of the discussion.
"What about the medicinal gardens?" she asked. "Will they allow an attendant inside?"
"Not the restricted gardens immediately. My residence has cultivation plots, and my status gives me access to ordinary medicinal grounds. You will begin there."
"Do they have anything related to the Earthmarrow fern?"
"Possibly. You are not asking anyone about a rare plant connected to another world on your first day."
Loriel looked offended. "I know that."
"You were about to ask."
"Only you."

By the time they finished, Vyra had filled twelve pages with terminology, hierarchy, forms of address, and the limits of Leon’s token. She also insisted that everyone carry ordinary local clothing and possessions rather than items that might invite questions.

Preparing to leave made the decision real in a way the discussion had not. Seraphine packed quickly and kept only what she could carry without a storage artifact. Ira complained about wrapping her spear, then redid the cloth herself when the first covering looked too conspicuous. Loriel spent nearly an hour arranging care for the quarantine plot and explaining the Earthmarrow fern’s schedule to three different gardeners. Vyra checked all four sets of belongings before allowing anyone to close them.
Leon watched without hurrying them. They had been ready in cultivation. Leaving the place that had sheltered them was a different kind of preparation.
The following morning, Leon returned alone to Jade Moon Palace.
Ji Liansu received him in the same quiet hall where she had examined the first stage of his Scripture. Her gaze passed once over his channels before settling on his face.
"You recovered quickly."
"The damage is closed. I will not resume experimentation until the remaining strain fades."
"Good. What do you need?"

Leon placed his direct-disciple token on the table between them. "Four attendants connected to my sealed inheritance have reached a nearby port. They survived the same secret realm and remained behind while I established a secure identity. I want to register them under my token."

Ji Liansu knew that Leon came from a lower-ranked world. She also knew the sealed-inheritance explanation protected facts he did not intend to share. As she had promised before, she did not ask him to expose those facts now.
"Their cultivation?" she asked.
"All four are Peak Foundation Establishment. Their methods are unusual but stable."
"Their roles?"
Leon listed them.
Ji Liansu considered the request for a moment, then touched one finger to the token. A pale crescent appeared on its surface.

"This authorizes four personal attendants under your responsibility," she said. "The gate officials will record their names, cultivation, and duties. Their origins will be registered under the same sealed-realm protection as yours. I will not permit anyone to investigate beyond that without bringing the request to me."
"Thank you."
"Do not thank me yet. Their conduct will reflect on you, and yours will determine how closely the Palace watches them."
Leon thought of Ira asking whether she could fight anyone.
"Understood."
Ji Liansu’s eyes narrowed slightly. "That answer lacked confidence."
"One of them is enthusiastic."
"Then I look forward to discovering whether your judgment is better in attendants than it is in duels."
Leon collected the token and left before she found another way to make the point.

By afternoon, he had descended to the nearest port under Jade Moon Palace authority and rented a small courtyard using his token. He inspected every formation himself, added two seals of his own, and confirmed that the property possessed no hidden observation array.
Only then did he enter the dimensional world.

The four women were waiting with their belongings packed in plain local cloth. Seraphine wore her sword openly. Ira had wrapped her spear but looked tempted to remove the covering. Vyra carried the book of notes beneath one arm, while Loriel held a small case of medicinal tools against her chest.

"Everything is approved," Leon said. "You will be registered under my token, and Ji Liansu has extended my sealed-realm protection to your origins. We appear in the port, walk to the Palace openly, and enter through the front gate."
Vyra nodded. Ira straightened with immediate interest. Loriel looked nervous but did not step back.
Seraphine came to Leon’s side. "And after the gate?"
"After the gate, you stop waiting for my visits and live there with me."
Her expression softened.
Leon looked at all four of them. They had crossed one world at his side, spent more than ten months building foundations for another, and reached the point he had once expected to take years.
"It is time," he said.
He opened the passage.
Cold, dense mana flowed into the dimensional world. Beyond the full standing gateway waited the quiet courtyard of the port, its stone walls silver beneath the higher world’s moonlight.
No one crossed yet.
Together, they looked through.
